reviews.snippet: Truth is I'm not a big fan of Greek food but hubby is. My dinner was eh, while he said his was OK, not great. The grape leaves were delicious and the baklava was devine. Hubby wanted beer but it was all sold out 2 days ago at Easter and the new delivery was late. He also wanted the rice pudding for dessert but that was also sold out. Service was great and restraunt was clean

response.snippet: Thank you so much for your review!

reviews.snippet: We were there in December and came across Symposium while walking. We were impressed by the cozy atmosphere and the amazing service we received. Our server knew a lot about the history of the restaurant and was helpful in suggesting a wine with dinner. The hummus, lemon potatoes and steamed vegetables were all very savory! I highly recommend and we will be back next time in NYC!

response.snippet: Thank you very much for your wonderful review!

reviews.snippet: This is my first time trying local Greek food as I had a favorite in Brooklyn that closed during the pandemic. Symposium will be my new go to spot. The service was excellent and the food was delicious.

response.snippet: We’re so happy you enjoyed the flavors and felt the Greek spirit in every bite. With gratitude, Symposium Greek Restaurant

reviews.snippet: We walked in on a Monday night, was seated fast. Decor was nice. Noise level was decent. Good came out quick. Waiter was good. The food was delicious. Took the soup to go, and was excellent. The food wasnt greasy. The plates were huge, so the price to food portion was a good value. We had some Mythos and Alfa beers. It felt like we were sitting back in Santorini on a late night dinner date.

response.snippet:
Raymond,

It’s wonderful hearing that your evening brought back the spirit of Greece in both atmosphere and taste.

With appreciation,
Symposium Greek Taverna

reviews.snippet:
We had dinner at Symposium for the first time tonight and everything was wonderful. Our favorites were the octopus, the mezze sampler (especially the tirokafteri), and the classic moussaka. The flavors had the perfect home cooked depth, true Greek classics.

The vibe is homey and cozy, great for a group of friends or families. We had the nicest servers, Alex and Elena, and we appreciated their hospitality.

The portion sizes were also generous and even though we were stuffed I’m glad we made room for dessert and Greek coffee- definitely recommend the galaktoboureko.

We will be coming back for sure!

response.snippet: Claire, it was a pleasure serving you and thank you for rating and sharing your experience at Symposium!

reviews.snippet:
Highly Highly Highly recommended! The general vibe of the restaurant feels homey and cozy, the staff is very nice, and most importantly; the food is delicious! The portions are big so you won't leave hungry!
They also have a special selection of wines that I recommend to try!
It's located close to the 1 train (Colombia University) so getting there is not a problem at all.
I definitely will be coming back!!

response.snippet: Vika, thanks for the review and the highlighting of your favorites!

reviews.snippet: This restaurant is definitely one of those jewels! It’s filled with eclectic artwork and the owners are super passionate about all the history of the space. It’s such a cozy spot. They are so warm and welcoming too!! There’s a hidden secret garden that’s so cool. The place is like a treasure chest! The food is delicious! They have so much to choose from. I think my favorites are the Pastitio, the Spicy Feta Dip, The Chicken Kebab, Meatballs… well I guess I just love everything! The wine is perfect too! This place is great for groups or parties or an intimate date night!

response.snippet: Thank you for your review and sharing your meal!

reviews.snippet: This place USED to be the absolute best Greek food in NYC. It was legendary. Now, the food is completely different and it is quite poor. The caviar dip was so light and wonderful and now it is a gooey, unappetizing mess. The pastitsio is covered in tomato sauce and now tastes Italian. The moussaka is just not what it was before. The pita was undercooked and flat. It used to be the absolute best. Will forever miss the old Symposium, with that wonderful , friendly man who ran the place.

response.snippet: Thank you for reviewing us!

reviews.snippet:
Ate at this historic restaurant with a friend who works at Columbia nearby . The space itself is incredibly beautiful. One of the loveliest and most welcoming spaces I’ve ever experienced in a restaurant. Service was also great and I appreciate that they chill the water in the ice bucket with the white wine so it comes to the table refreshingly cold.

The food was ok. We both got the puréed potato and beet appetizer which was excellent. My friend got a lamb burger that he really liked. I got the chicken souvlaki which was nothing to write home about. Both were part of a lunch special deal.

The table beside us got saganaki and a whole fish. That looked like a better meal, though I’m sure it cost more.

In short, I would go back but probably order something not on the lunch special menu.

response.snippet:
Stuart,
Thanks for sharing your thoughts an reviewing our restaurant!
We are looking forward to serving you in the future!
Best!

reviews.snippet: If you are a fan of Greek food this place is the one ! Amazing food and outstanding service, Elena and Nino are very nice and professional. We loved every single thing we tried from Dips platter to grilled calamari, chicken gyro lamb souvlaki and lamb shank. The wine , the beers and the sangria are also delicious. I would recommend this place to everyone. Thank you Symposium for an amazing dinner.

response.snippet: Thank you very much for revieweing us!

Love the ambiance there, which is perfect for date night in a nice, quiet area of the city. I would recommend Symposium to anyone and EVERYONE!! Superb Greek cuisine and the sangria is delish!!

reviews.snippet: This restaurant is reminiscent of old style New York City homes with brick walls, wooden panels, and low lit environment. The service Sunday evening was excellent and delightful. The meal was delicious and well served.

response.snippet: Thank you very much for reviewing us!

reviews.snippet:
The $27 lunch special was well worth it, especially for a restaurant in Manhattan near to Columbia University.

The meat quality was quite good and the so were the sides.

I've been eating at Symposium for 29 years - at least once a year and, on many years, multiple times. My favorite Greek restaurant anywhere. You must must get the mixed-salad appetizer. Along with the warm pita that comes with it - I can eat this dish any day, every day!

response.snippet: Thank you very much for rating us and sharing with the others!

reviews.snippet: The inside of this restaurant felt capacious and cavernous. I must admit that I found it a little bit dark and isolating. But that's less a fault of the restaurant than a consequence of my being there by myself at around 3:00 in the afternoon. As for the food, it was fine. I had the lamb. It was neither the best nor the worst lamb I've had in my life. Portions were reasonably sized, and the price was reasonable. I have few explicit complaints, except that I want more than the simply adequate when I choose to go out to eat. So I'm giving three stars, though I admit that had I come here with a large party at around 7:00 or 8:00 at night, the atmosphere would have felt much more soothing and bustlingly alive.

response.snippet: Thank you, for sharing your experience!

I recommend the Lavraki fillet and Youvetsi Me Keftedes.

reviews.snippet: The food is top notch delicious! Our waiter Chris was super helpful and answered all questions. He even let us taste 3 different wines before choosing the wine we liked! Highly recommend trying this place out you won't be disappointed. 👍🏻

Had a couple of bottles of wine that they got for us even though it was close to closing. We rushed ourselves out so they weren’t waiting on us, but we never felt rushed by the staff. Again, delicious food ! Kind staff.

reviews.snippet: We had lunch. The dishes are pretty big, sharing a small symposyum as an appetizer and asking a souvlaki lamb then, I was completely full, even though I was pretty hungry. Anastasio, the server, makes you feel like you’re in a truly greek restaurant, given his knowledge of each dish and his greek soul. My brother and his girlfriend ordered a chicken gyro platter each, which was also really big and yummy. We were three and spent a total of $67. I’ll definitely come back.

response.snippet: Thank you very much for sharing your experience and reviewing us!

reviews.snippet: WOW!!! Best spinach pie ever! My wife spent time living in Greece and ate a spinach pie every day for lunch. She has been trying to find a similar pie for me to enjoy since I was not there. We have had spinach pies from the West coast to NYC. Here we found the best she has ever had and me as well. It was huge, thick, full of fresh spinach and cheese, flaky outside, hot, and served with style! Thank you!

response.snippet: Thanks vor visiting, we are glad that you had enjoyed our spinach pie!

reviews.snippet: I loved this place. The staff treated us so well and the food was so amazing. My husband and I both got the beef gyro combo plate and it was awesome. They put literal pieces of steak in it, which is so good. Also, I love the inside of the restaurant--I think it looks cool. Highly recommend this place if you like good Greek/Mediterranean food.

So it was my first time eating at a Greek restaurant and it was with a big group of around 16. The owner was super nice to us, so we got to try the pita bread and a light dish for free. Everything was really good :) love their chicken gyro!
Everything is amazing about this spot. A hidden gem. Food is delicious, service is great, prices are good, and atmosphere is amazing.

It means a lot to know you enjoyed both the food and the welcoming vibe here.

All our gratitude,
Symposium Greek Restaurant

Terrible experience. Made a reservation yesterday (for today), received multiple confirmations, showed up to find the restaurant closed/under construction. The workers there called the owner who angrily shouted "Can't you see the sign says it's closed?" I told him we had a reservation, but before I could proceed he hung up. Not even an apology. I used to love this restaurant years ago but will never go back.

response.snippet:
Hi Karina,

We’re truly sorry for your recent experience. Although we shut down our reservation system, it appears that your booking accidentally went through. Unfortunately, we’ve been closed since last Friday due to a gas leak.

I also apologize if I spoke a bit loudly when my employee called me—I was in the subway at the time and wish our conversation had taken place under better circumstances.

We hope you’ll consider rebooking your dinner with us soon so we can show you the genuine hospitality we’re known for.
Wishing you happy holidays and all the best,
Chef Dan/Owner

reviews.snippet:
Recently, my wife and I discovered Symposium, a hidden gem in North Manhattan, while driving home. Its Greek sign beckoned us into an experience reminiscent of the cozy taverns in Athens, where entering feels like stepping into a secret cave or basement. Celebrating Greece’s Independence Day and the Feast of the Annunciation on March 25th, we were delighted by the traditional dishes that paid homage to these significant events, much like the celebrations back home in Greece.

The highlight of our meal was the cod with garlic spread (μπακαλιάρο σκορδαλιά), a signature dish for the day, embodying the essence of Greek tradition. Our feast also included crispy octopus, kalamarakia, French fries sprinkled with feta, shrimp saganaki, a refreshing Greek salad, authentic Greek coffee, portokalopita, and the sublime galaktoboureko. Each dish transported us to Greece with its authentic flavors, as if homemade.

Accompanied by a “Savvatiano” crisp, cold white Greek wine, served in an ice bucket to maintain its chill, the dining experience was elevated. The staff’s politeness and hospitality added to the warmth of the evening, and the generous aperitif of Samos wine from the manager before our departure was a gracious touch.

Symposium stands out not just for its genuine Greek cuisine but also for being the sole authentic Greek restaurant above 110th Street in North Manhattan, making it a perfect choice for our family. We are grateful for the memorable evening and look forward to returning. Thank you, Symposium, for a wonderful dining experience. Until next time.

Junzi Kitchen exceeds my expectations. They say that they serve Asian food with a twist, that sounded weird to me, but I still went. When you walk inside, you notice how nice, and modern the decor is! Let's see what they have! You walk up to the large counter (where you order) and you notice that they have a lot of stuff, what should I have? What is really unique about Junzi Kitchen is that you can customize your noodles or wrap to fit your personal taste, I find that really nice. You are next in line. The employee behind the counter looks at you, she or he says "Pick the type of noodle you want" or something like that. You keep moving along, you pick your noodle, your meat, your sauce, your vegetables, and then there is also sauce at the end of the counter. Once you pick those, 🔎you find a table. You will probably find a table, if you do not, you can take your noodles out, because you have plastic wrapped around your bowl of noodles. Junzi Kitchen is inexpensive.

I RECOMMEND:

I recommend having the chili sauce, it makes the noodles taste so good!

I recommend getting one of the soda's for a drink, they taste really good!

reviews.snippet:
This restaurant knows what it is doing. I will admit I didn't give it much thought when it first opened but it has been expanding and I was stuck in the rain. I figure why not. Sometimes life has a funny way of working out.

Junzi is respectful of traditional flavors but also does a great job of adding a modern flare to the menu. It's approachable for those unfamiliar with the flavors. Their choices are noodles or bings which are similar to wraps.

I opted for noodles during this visit, furu chicken with a side of extra beef shank. It's like guacamole, worth the extra charge. The chicken was shredded and pretty flavorful. It was a touch dry but with the sauces, it wasn't too bad. The sesame sauce wasn't too overwhelming. I prefer a stronger sesame taste but I love sesame. It's creamy but not too saucy, just enough to coat each strand of noodle. There are several choices for noodles. Rice noodles was the one that came with the order but I might try the knife cut noodles. It might be better to hold up against the sauce and have a nicer chew. The rice noodles were less springy. Get all the veggies that are offered. They add freshness and a crunchy texture to the dish. They are also just so simple but good. The flavors of the veggies themselves have a moment to shine.

Now about those beef shank, these were spot on. They were so tender but not overcooked. They still had a nice beefiness but a nice touch of savory and a just a very hint of sweet, so subtle but so well balanced.

The chili paste should definitely be added to the noodles. It's not just simply an addition of heat but there is smokiness to it. It's crispy which adds another texture to the noodles. So you will get creaminess from the sauce, crunchy from the veggies and crispy bits from the chili paste/oil.

My order of noodles were such a delight and I would happily come back even when I am not stuck in the rain and Uber is surging. The service is also so friendly. They are friendly and so patient as I decided what I wanted. Thanks for being a ray of sunshine when it was pouring outside.

reviews.snippet: Tom’s Restaurant was at the top of my bucket list as a Seinfeld fan for 3 decades. The iconic front for Monk’s Diner from the show was everything I wanted it to be and more! The staff were amazing, quick, kind and fun. The coffee was classic, booths were comfy, super cute bar top, and it has an adorable outside patio on a great side of town. Lots of memorabilia from the show and epic photo opportunities for fans. We both ordered BIG Salads and they were fresh and fantastic! Highly recommend for great food and atmosphere. Loved their fries, SO yum! Lots of menu options, yada, yada, yada. 🤣

The chicken cutlet was tasty, but the pasta and sauce had no flavor at all, it honestly tasted like plain crushed tomatoes. I even added some salt and pepper myself, but it didn’t help much. We ordered the steak medium, but it came out well-done.

That said, the atmosphere was nice and the diner itself was beautiful, and all the staff were very kind and friendly.

Came because of Seinfeld and was worried it might be a tourist trap (crowded, overpriced, etc.). I couldn’t have been more wrong. The food was genuinely very good, and the place felt like a true local diner despite its fame. This was actually my second visit. Earlier this year I stopped by for a chicken menu that was also excellent, so it was nice to see that the quality wasn’t a one-off.

The service was excellent, especially from the Hispanic server who looked after us- she was spectacular. My Eggs Benedict were OK, but I tried several dishes from around the table and they were all outstanding. The cheeseburger was particularly delicious.

If you are a fan of classic television, Tom's Restaurant is an absolute must-visit in New York City. This iconic spot is famous for serving as the exterior of the diner in Seinfeld. While the interior doesn't perfectly match the show since those scenes were filmed on a Hollywood soundstage, stepping inside still offers a quintessential, nostalgic American diner experience.

The restaurant is wonderfully decorated with genuine Seinfeld memorabilia, including authentic autographs from the original cast members. Even Jerry Seinfeld himself has visited!

Beyond the incredible pop culture history, the food and service truly stand on their own. The staff, along with the owner, are incredibly welcoming and friendly, making you feel right at home. I highly recommend saving room for dessert because their cheesecake is easily one of the best I have ever had. Additionally, the coffee is surprisingly excellent for a traditional New York diner.

Another major plus is their late-night hours, making it a great spot to grab an evening bite. Beware that the surrounding neighborhood can feel a little unsettled late at night, but that is entirely outside of the business's control. Overall, this is a fantastic establishment that delivers both on its legendary TV status and its high-quality food and service. Highly recommended!

Let’s be real, you’re not coming to Tom’s for the food, you’re coming here because of the show. And while Tom’s certainly caters to the fans by having a number of pictures of the cast, it’s functionally just a typical NYC diner. The Lumberjack was pretty decent

Location known to be iconic from the sitcom Seinfeld. Operates as a diner, but I would say service wise it does not operate as such and you will be rushed to order and eat in order to flip tables. I had the chicken parmigiana sandwich, expensive for the serving size but was alright.

Yummy and lovely diner near Columbia. Everything was very fairly priced and quite delicious. The chocolate chip pancakes in particular stood out and I was very grateful to the continuous refills of coffee. I also love the booth style seating, twas very nostalgic.

Was in NYC near Columbia University and was looking for a quick bite. Being a Seinfeld fan the restaurant caught my eye. I initially kept walking but something said to go in and check it out for the experience. Inside the restaurant it's got ~14-15 booths and counter seating (It's not laid out like on the TV show). I sat at the bar flipped through the menu and it was mostly diner food. They have Gyros also but I opted for the California Burger (lettuce, tomato and avocado) + fries and a coffee milkshake. My customer service experience was delivered in a gruff NYC style. He plopped the menu down in front of me. He came back 5 minutes later… “You know what you want”. I still needed a minute…he walked away. I signaled I was ready, gave him my order, he said “ok”, then placed the order over the microphone (which reminded me of the old “Olympia Restaurant” skit on SNL). This is the typical “lets keep it moving” type of service that I grew up with in NYC.

The burger and fries were nothing to write home about. The shake was the best part. The coolest part was seeing all the Seinfeld memorabilia. Would I come back again….likely not. I would only recommend this spot if you are a Seinfeld fan or you were in the area and wanted diner food.

Very quick service I went at about 9am. Had the lumberjack, eggs over easy and with pancakes. I served it with whipped butter and maple syrup. Bacon was crispy, pancakes were fluffy, eggs were runny and the sausage was bouncy. Overall very good 👍 I ordered the chocolate egg cream. It did not contain any egg or cream and tasted like watered down fizzy chocolate milkshake. For $6 it was not worth it. Hence knocked 1 star off. The lumberjack was good about $17 or so.
It looks different inside than I expected and was very popular at lunch time. The staff were fast and friendly and I liked the food. I would come here again.
Back after 15 years, and it brought back so many memories. I used to come here all the time after class. Such a classic, legit American diner experience.

Now, decided to give it a second chance (as I love Seinfeld), came for lunch, plenty 2 person tables, they pointed me to counter sits, saying that at lunch they don't want to give me a table for two. We had the eggs Benedict and it was pretty good. The corned beef omelette however was a little dry. Ambience is typical diner style with a bar and stools. Popular dining place for the Columbia students.
It's a fun and iconic place to stop for any Seinfeld fan, but the food was just alright. Breakfast served all day is always nice and the service / atmosphere was great.

This place is super iconic because of Seinfeld, but the inside isn’t really what you’d expect — it’s different, but still feels authentic and really cool. It’s got a chill, college vibe, probably because it’s so close to Columbia University. The food was good, the service was nice, and overall it was just a really fun spot to check out.

It’s Seinfeld’s restaurant. As a huge Seinfeld fan, this place was a must visit for me. A cozy, slow paced and charming American diner with a really welcoming atmosphere. My wife had a coffee and I grabbed a beer since I don’t drink coffee or soda. The man behind the counter was very friendly, and the Seinfeld photo memorabilia throughout the place was a great touch.

I had a late lunch here. I think many people come for the experience, as the exterior was used as the site of the restaurant in Seinfeld. It is a fun New York joint with people packed in and a lot of yelling. You really need to come and be a part of history.I had coffee (why is diner coffee so bad), one fried egg, toast, potatoes, and hash for $17, which is pretty good for NYC prices.

Visiting Tom’s Restaurant during my trip to New York was a surprisingly emotional experience. As a long-time fan of Seinfeld, standing in front of the iconic facade—unchanged since the show aired—immediately brought back memories of scenes and laughs from one of the most legendary sitcoms of all time. It felt surreal to be there in person after seeing it so many times on screen.

Beyond Seinfeld, Tom’s Restaurant holds another cultural significance—it’s famously referenced in Suzanne Vega’s song “Tom’s Diner”. Knowing that this humble little diner has inspired such pop culture moments made being there feel even more special.

Inside, the atmosphere is classic, no-frills New York diner: friendly staff, fast service, and a cozy, down-to-earth vibe. I had a simple breakfast—eggs, toast, and coffee—and it was just right. It’s not about gourmet food, it’s about the nostalgia and the feeling of being connected to something bigger than just a meal.

If you're visiting New York and have even the slightest appreciation for TV history or music, Tom’s Restaurant is absolutely worth the stop. It’s more than just a diner—it’s a piece of American pop culture that still stands strong.

Title: A Classic Delight at Tom's Restaurant: A Seinfeld Experience

Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

I recently had the pleasure of visiting Tom's Restaurant in New York City, and as a fan of Seinfeld, it was an experience filled with nostalgia and culinary delight. Located on the corner of West 112th Street and Broadway, this iconic eatery has been serving up delicious meals since 1940, and it truly lives up to its reputation.

Atmosphere:
Stepping inside Tom's Restaurant felt like entering the pages of a Seinfeld episode. The walls adorned with quirky memorabilia and familiar photographs instantly transported me back to the beloved sitcom. The cozy and vibrant interior, combined with the buzzing energy of fellow diners, created an atmosphere that was both comfortable and lively.

Service:
The staff at Tom's Restaurant were friendly, accommodating, and efficient. Despite the restaurant being busy on a Friday night, our server greeted us with a warm smile and promptly took our orders. Throughout our meal, they ensured that we had everything we needed, and their attention to detail added to the overall positive experience.

Food:
Now, let's talk about the star of the show—the food! Tom's Restaurant offers a diverse menu featuring classic American comfort food, and we indulged in a variety of dishes. The burgers were juicy, flavorful, and cooked to perfection, satisfying even the most discerning burger connoisseur. The pancakes were fluffy and accompanied by a generous serving of maple syrup, making for a delightful breakfast-for-dinner experience. As for the mozzarella sticks and chicken fingers, they were crispy on the outside, tender on the inside, and served with a side of tangy dipping sauces that enhanced their taste.

Value:
Considering the quality and portion sizes, the prices at Tom's Restaurant were reasonable, aligning with the average prices in the area. The affordability of the meals made the dining experience even more enjoyable, as we left with satisfied appetites and wallets.

Conclusion:
Tom's Restaurant is not just a place to have a meal; it's an iconic New York City landmark that encapsulates the nostalgia of Seinfeld. The friendly atmosphere, attentive service, and delectable food make it a must-visit for both fans of the show and food enthusiasts alike. Whether you're craving a burger, pancakes, or a taste of the Seinfeld universe, Tom's Restaurant will not disappoint. Make sure to visit, and prepare to create your own memorable dining experience.

Remember, "No soup for you!"
Went for Seinfeld vibes and got to click a pic with Tom Cruise.. haha 😂 great food, good people, fantastic memory of NYC ❤️

We're big Seinfeld fans, so made the pilgrimage here. We really liked the vibe! Of course, we knew that the show wasn't actually filmed inside here, but it was still fun to visit and had a nice dinner. The waiter was warm and friendly, and my Greek salad hit the spot.

Customer since 1963 ! Was student at Columbia University.. plus I am Seinfeld fan to boot. Food is consistently well prepared.The service staff are great and almost always helpful. A Manhattan ICON. Kramer could walk in at any moment! GOOD EATS.

Awe man, i can't tell you how excited I was to come here. The very restaurant the Jerry Seinfeld was taped. Seinfeld is my favorite sitcom. The food, service, and atmosphere were excellent! I got the Ruben Pastrami sandwich and it was delicious. I'm from El Paso TX.

If you’re hoping that the inside of this diner looks like the diner on Seinfeld, it doesn’t. With that said, the service is great! There are a few mentions of Seinfeld on the menu like Jerry’s Big Salad, not Elaine’s Big Salad, it’s called Jerry’s Big Salad. The pancakes are great. Omelette was over cooked and house potatoes lacked flavor. They have some souvenirs in relation to Seinfeld. For the Seinfeld fan, it’s a must.

Intrigue to visit cause we were rewatching Seinfeld! Definitely worth visiting.. more for the fans of the show.. *just the outside is the same though.. inside is totally different.. there are lots of memorabilias from the show inside.. food is good and service as well! Price not too bad being in NY ..

This is a must if you are a Seinfeld fan. The outside looks exactly like the series one did.
I had a bagel with lox and cream cheese and coffee and both were delicious.
Very good service and clean bathrooms. Close to the Subway in case you are far away! Don't miss this chance to get your big salad 😉
Loved the place. It still keeps the original style of dinners vibe from the early 80's Memorabilia of Seinfeld us nice. The food was good and not expensive.

Came in briefly to get a souvenir for my dad from Seinfeld, the outside was beautiful and was exactly like the show and inside they have really cute memorabilia- but the reason for the lower rating is because both bathrooms were out of service and all credit card machines were down so we had to wait 30 minutes to pay. But really cute place and worth visiting if you’re a Seinfeld fan!

I was watching this show on Netflix and got curious about visiting one of the famous spots appeared in the show. Well, I wasn’t expecting that, it is all show’s oriented and themed! I’m glad I went. Food is good, nothing special, still a regular diner but had a good experience. Watch Seinfeld then go here, thank me later

Went here for my friends who wanted to dine at the Seinfeld diner. I liked that they kept the diner feel and you could get classic diner fare even including a banana split! The service could be improved but there was nonwair tingwt a table and all in all it was a fun experience and definitely worth a visit ad a new York landmark.
Was the song “Tom’s Diner” written about this place?

I love that this place exists because it's a historical landmark. Having a physical space for Seinfeld fans to visit is lovely. The memorabilia was great. Just wish the food was better. Had eggs Benny, wish they asked what I wanted for a side. I don't like hash browns. I would have preferred a salad or fruit. There is room to improve, but I'll say it again, I'm so happy this restaurant exists.

It was good. It's really one of the most famous diner in New York City, but the food wasn't as much good. Toasts were not done right. Coffee was too good though.
Wall with all country's currencies was a nice thing.
It's famous for "Seinfeld". With increase in fame its food quality is decreased.

I visited because of Seinfeld, but you shouldn't just take a photo of the outside, as they serve great food here! I went for a hot turkey sandwich with a generous side of cranberry. The cherry pie for dessert was delicious, unfortunately I wasn't able to finish it all. Damn fine coffee too!

A classic diner with friendly staff and a huge selection of comfort food! You'll find Seinfeld posters and magazines all over the place, reminding you that the diner was once used as the show's restaurant spot. Prices are fair for the size of the food you get, and I can see myself going there again to try out more from the menu.

Feels surreal eating here when you’re a big fan of seinfeld. Staff was attentive, decor was nice and had lots of pictures from the cast, plus other pics of famous people eating there. Great experience!

Iconic diner located on the ground floor of Columbia's Armstrong Hall. It was featured in popular sitcom Seinfeld and frequented by many famous figures. You can find typical diner items on the menu. Prices were fair and food was very good. The atmosphere is really authentic! Fully recommended!
Always great. Of course it's fame grew b/c of Seinfeld, but the place been around long before that. It's an Institution and the new manager is awesome!
Best diner in Brooklyn. They were so accommodating of our large group with luggage. The service and the overall vibe were incredibly warm. Putting this on my list of “definitely go back” gems.
I had three big salad just like Elaine. Finn place to eat. Staff was fantastic

I have walked past Toms for years, and I was finally able to give it a try. I love an old-school dinner location. It is a tight space inside, but the service is really quick. I ordered a chicken tender meal which came with french fries and chicken noodle soup. The soup was nostalgic and the tenders were okay. I really liked the mozzarella sticks. The cheese pull was 10/10, and they reminded me of some old-school fresh mozz sticks. You get 6. The fries were also decent as well - 6.5/10.

Cool diner located on the ground floor of Columbia's Armstrong Hall. It was featured in popular sitcom Seinfeld and frequented by many famous figures. You can find typical diner items on the menu. Prices were fair and food was average. The atmosphere deserves a 5 star rating - many photographs and knick knacks on the wall for you to check out.

Seinfeld diner, had to take my sister who is a fanatic. Interior and atmosphere is nice and lively, bustling with lots of students. The waitress did irk me a bit as I was looking through the menu. We said we needed a few more minutes and she came back every 15 seconds to ask if we were ready, but she was lovely. At the end I just chose anything I saw because I felt immensely pressured and so did my sister. My boyfriend got a corner beef Reuben which he says was fine, I got a corned beef sandwich which was terribly dry, and my sister got standard eggs and turkey bacon platter. Don’t get the corned beef sandwich, I felt like throwing water on it so it could at least not feel like I’m eating beef jerky.
A must if you're a Seinfeld fan. Food is pretty good too and the staff are nice. There's some merch you can buy too.

Iconic from its inclusion in Seinfeld- Tom’s restaurant interior isn’t actually anything like the show sadly, but they do have a great and diverse breakfast and lunch menu served all day, and it’s very reasonable!

Thank you Tom's, not only did I have the pleasure of spending $13 for a $0.75 dollars worth of instant pasta, you didn't forget to have racist waiters on the side for the ultimate "screw you" experience I could have had.

I couldn't help but to notice the happier tone in the waiter's voice when she greeted with & talked to white people.

People of color know what I'm talking about.

It's a shame, because it's a cool place to be.

Other people who come here who is a PoC, maybe you can tell the obvious drop in her mood or her dismissive tone she wears when talking to a non-white.

Oh, want to pay your bill as a colored person? Good luck and hope that your host doesn't ignore you for 10 minutes so you have to walk out with payment on the table.

Honestly, I would have preferred that she turned us away. Save us the trouble of dealing with dehumanizing attitudes and overpriced and flavorless pasta.

It's sad that their garbage food is being sold at a premium because Seinfeld was shot here. Don't get me wrong, I expected flavorless food, I just didn't want to pay money to be treated like a 2nd class citizen.

is it an Eastern European thing? Idk

The food here was fantastic. Theee outside still looks like it did in the tv series Seinfeld, but the inside has been remodeled. You can buy cereal here as well just like Jerry did in the show. There is also tuna on toast which was one of George's regular orders. Worth checking out!

Seated quickly for an iconic restaurant-thought it may be busier. Order taken promptly and food came quickly. Hot and fresh. Nothing fancy, just a good old style diner. Food and iced tea were good. Had the Rancho Wrap. Would come back!

A fantastic and unique New Yorkian breakfast experience.

The food was reasonably priced and very tasty. The only problem I had was, as a British person, I didn't vibe with their potatoes.

But the service was delightful, the atmosphere was buzzing, and as a Seinfeld fan it was fantastic.
I went to Tom's specifically for it's Seinfeld roots. What I didn't expect was the quick service and very good diner food. I generally do not like Sausage Links but theirs were great.

Be nice or leave. Great sign staring back at you from the other side of the counter. And they are. Neat little diner on Broadway with a mixed menu. They have a great twist on the American classic with the Pizza Burger. Delicious. And the shakes are worth it on their own. Stop by this little joint that once was the stop for Seinfeld and company.

Really happy to have crossed this of my bucket list. Tom's Restaurant has a historical significance for me as a Seinfeld fan.
Besides that, the food was delicious - try "Jerry's Salad", and the hospitality of the staff exceeded my expectations.

Came here for breakfast on a Saturday because it’s “the Seinfeld diner!!” The food was a great deal and the staff were so nice. The walls have cool posters and media related to Seinfeld. It’s a super convenient location to get to (aka accessible by subway, as tourists) and the food came very fast.

Went here for the first time today and had some of the best tasting pancakes I've ever had. They were light, fluffy, sweet, and moist. My Dad had the salad and he really enjoyed it! The food was very tasty and fresh and the service was top notch! The staff was super friendly and kind. The place is small but has some serious charm.

Good diner — prices are pretty reasonable considering the location. Service was great and very fast, and my gyro was really good. The pita was excellent, the fries were perfect, the tzatziki was very good, but the meat itself was flavorful but dry.

Ordered from here Nov 8th. I was looking for a restaurant that was decently priced in regards to open face sandwiches. They were the only one who were under $20. In fact it was a little under 17. I ordered take out and got an open-face turkey sandwich . You get plenty of food. Honestly you can split between two people if you had to. And it was delicious to boot.
Staff were nice and pick up was easy!
Misc: I know most folks know about this place because of Seinfeld but I will always think of the Suzanne Vega song with this place
The Seinfeld restaurant. In the inside it’s a regular diner but has tons of Seinfeld memorabilia around. There was a short wait. Definitely worth a stop if you are fan.

While most other places conform to the modern trends, this small and comfortable place seems to have maintained its traditional style - small, independent, local and with employees who are down to earth.
Our server was very nice and welcomed my family. All our questions were put at ease with their personalities and the place's warm & friendly atmosphere. Our Food was optionally portioned for family sizes, intended for sharing. Food was warm and very filling. Even our deserts were nice and served wih a smile.
The atmosphere of this place is simple & American, with the old NY we all miss and adore at its core.

media.caption: Lemon pound bread, best in the area.
Breakfast for dinner - suasage and egg in a criossant.
Sliced turkey with vegetables, gravy, stuffing and cranberry jelly.

reviews.snippet: I have been visiting Tom's for a while when I'm in Morningside Heights. The service and ambiance are excellent. The food is pretty darn good, but it's my only reason for leaving four instead of five stars. Tom's has typical NYC or even slightly higher prices. I know the place is a draw because it's the "Seinfeld" restaurant. Again, I like the food there, but I just can't give it five stars. Tom's is an excellent spot to drop into after you're done walking around Columbia and checking out St. John's.
It's definitely not a restaurant about nothing. The food is amazing, and you can even get a big salad 🥗 This is a must for all Seinfeld fans. Also, check out Singfeld.

This is definitely the place!

The food is good. The people are good. The servers are nice and they’re friendly!

If you’re a Seinfeld fan, this is Paradise!

Got a burger for takeout it was delicious. We were passing through on our way to Long island and had to stop (big Seinfeld fans!) The guy working there was SO nice and everything was clean and great. Cheesecake for dessert and it was amazing. Had our dog with us otherwise we would have stayed and ate there. Will be back!
Great Place!! The bar tenders are incredibles. Good food and Seinfeld spirits

I just came here cuz of Seinfeld but i got an great experience
Service is excellent, food is so delicious, very fresh and great quality, prices are perfect
I really enjoyed a lot feels like i was in a Seinfeld episode 👏🏻👏🏻
My wife and I are huge Seinfeld fans. We visited NYC to celebrate her birthday weekend and had to drop in to have lunch at Tom's. It was fun and the food was great.

Tom's Diner is an amazing place that offers the best NYC neighborhood diner experience. One of my favorites here is the hot coffee served in a cup that never goes dry or gets cold, which is perfect for coffee lovers like me. In addition, they have not just one, but two bathrooms for customers, ensuring convenience and comfort during visits. The staff is incredibly friendly and efficient, providing excellent service. And let's not forget about the food - it is absolutely delicious. Overall, Tom's Diner is a must-visit for anyone looking for a memorable and satisfying dining experience.

media.caption: French toast, turkey bacon, sunny side up egg over easy, endless hot coffee

reviews.snippet:
Ordered food through Uber Eats with a bunch of people a couple weeks ago. The food got here timely, but most of the food recieved was overpriced, very low quality and IMO they should be embarrassed for serving it. The worst example was the fish and chips, hockey puck of a fish stick with the most bland 'chips' ever (and they don't come with malt vinegar). Take your pic in front of the place if you like Seinfeld then go a couple blocks to Mel's if you want a great burger or Metro Diner if you want better diner food.

Cannot speak of the staff or the atmosphere since I haven't been inside in years.

The staff were very kind, helpful and fast. This is an iconic diner for all us Seinfeld fans. The diner is filled with the show's memorabilia, and we loved the versatility of the menu, from sandwiches, pancakes to specialties of all sorts. Still, be aware the location is high north over Central Park, but it waa worth the walk.

What’s the deal with classic East Coast diners? Their the perfect breakfast, especially after a night of bar hopping the city. Found myself here mainly because I’m a Seinfeld fan but the food is solid. Great eggs, perfect potatoes and fantastic corn beef hash. Wash it down with some OJ and a classic slice of New York cheesecake. The waitress was friendly and the service was quick, truly a classic diner experience. A couple of cups of coffee later we were now ready to hoof it to Central Park. Well fed with good food for a great price and a cool photo opportunity, what’s not to like. Anyways yada yada yada dos thumbs up 👍👍
Classic NY Diner with friendly service and tasty food - definitely worth a visit if you are around. Really enjoyed the french toast.
Classic diner with special provenance of being the front for the Seinfeld diner. Service is quick! Eggs Benedict was top choice with the lumberjack breakfast second.

media.caption: Lumberjack. Over medium eggs with Bacon.

reviews.snippet: Amazing food, friendly staff, good atmosphere. A must stop for the Seinfeld fans. They also have a delicious pound cake and pies.

Oh come on! How can you go to Manhattan and not visit 'Monks' Cafe from Seinfeld! When I sat down the server told me they have the best chocolate milkshake and you know what? It really was.😋 Season 5 Episode 10 when Kramer just had to have the gyro when on the subway back from Frank and Estelle's house in Queens. I now understand why... so so sooooooo good. You gotta go to Tom's... you gotta go!

Our food tasted great and the waitress was very attentive. It wasn't too busy and there was plenty of seating inside. I recommend the BLT wrap. Lots of iconic Seinfeld memorabilia on the walls to look at too. This is a must see if you are a Seinfeld fan.

Unspectacular Restaurant - apparently famous from the Seinfeld series, which is why a friend wanted to go there and I joined. It serves the food of a typical new york diner, nothing special, but also nothing terrible. Had the fish and chips, my friend had a burger - both were OK, but not memorable. Fries that came with it were somewhat on the dry side, but not terrible either. Recommended if you are a fan of Seinfeld, or if you are in the area & in need of a quick and unspectacular bite.
Foodies on the hunt for NYCs most exciting cuisine (like myself) will be better off going somewhere else.

The staff are super personable. The french toast is astounding! The prices are also really competitive considering that the place is a bit of a landmark. They aren't hostile to tourists either is you're nervous about that! I came in when they were doing a breakfast special and got french toast with 2 huge scoops of ice cream plus a glass of orange juice for only 13$. The single best way to spend 13$ in all of NY! (of course it came out to more than 13, I had to tip generously with how kind they were!)
As a local guide i can honestly say this play has it all. Greasy spoon type drip and it’s from your favourite show. The servers were incredible wow five stars

Good diner food, fast and efficient service, although the place can get very busy.
It’s in close proximity to the Columbia University campus. Not open during the night.
This diner was featured from the outside on the Seinfeld show. Quite the NYC landmark.

media.caption: That looks familiar to many TV viewers

reviews.snippet: Relaxed, friendly, and efficient. The staff are excellent here. The food is also above average for diner fare. The lumberjack breakfast, with eggs, pancakes, sausage and bacon is a great deal. A good neighborhood joint.

Like most others, we came here because of Seinfeld. Lovely little diner with traditional American comfort food. Grabbed some coffee and a slice of cherry pie, which was delicious.
Staff were very friendly.
Overall a great experience!
If you’re a Seinfeld fan, you can’t miss Tom’s diner. After you get a selfie out the front, the food and service inside is decent. No ‘big salad’ on the menu but plenty other items to choose from.
Seinfeld buffs know it's here! Great location and typical diner menu in NYC .. fun decor based around the show. Food was very good (eggs and veggie burger)

Was with a group of people looking for something to eat at 5pm on a Friday and literally stumbled upon this place, immediately recognizable for obvious reasons (not that there’s anything wrong with that), and since I’ve most of our party was from out of town, of course we went in. It’s a great little diner, exactly what you would expect. Naturally I ordered the biggest burger on the menu, and this is the first time I’ve ever seen a double cheeseburger that is actually *TWO* separate burgers. No problem, easy enough to rectify with a little disassembly and reassembly. The before and after pictures speak for themselves. Burger was tasty and well prepared. Like I said, just what you would expect, a great little diner in Manhattan. I’d go back!
Tom's definitely the diner aviance. Good service good food. It was nice because we loved Seinfeld so we just wanted to have that experience. Easy to get to and find. The staff was kind.

Nothing out of the ordinary. Very classic styled diner; a no-frills spot. Don’t expect photographic meals if you’re into that kinda stuff or you ‘eat with your eyes.’ Went on a Sunday for brunch around 1pm and though it was crazy busy, we were seated pretty quickly. Service was prompt but they did forget my toast and even after mentioning it, I had to do another reminder after minutes had passed and I wasn’t served. It’s good for a typical quick bite, however.

media.caption: Far back: the combo (eggs, pancakes, bacon); Left side: Spinach omelette, potatoes, side of bacon

reviews.snippet: Very nice diner, food was wonderful, it is very good comfort food.

As a huge Seinfeld fan,this was a must stop. It obviously looks nothing like Monks on the inside but it's a cozy little diner with very attentive staff. Food was good and served quick. The coffee was strong and they have cool souvenir shirts that I had to have. Glad I made my way there.
Although the interior isn’t like the show, they lean into the Seinfeld connection well. Nice staff and very good food! Tuna melt was amazing!!!
The best pancakes I’ve had in all USA. Amazing choco shake. If you are a Seinfeld fan you’re gonna love this place. The service is quick. The Greek guy at the bar is very grumpy and funny.

If you are a Seinfeld fan, you don't need me to tell you that you have to go to Tom's restaurant. Just do it.

I spent a couple of hours there, having breakfast and having a couple of zoom calls.

The place is nice and the breakfast was ok. It was not the best in the world but hey, you can't have it all.

The atmosphere in this place is really nice, you feel like you are inside a Seinfeld episode...(not really).

In all seriousness, i like this place. The staff is nice and Louie is a nice guy too.

I bought a Tom's Restaurant mug for the second time. The first one broke while changing houses. Not that you need to know all this.

Anyway, just go there.

Cheers.

Authentic American diner. Fabulous food at proper prices and the service was typically great. Came here as a Seinfeld fan but it's so much more than the neon sign. We had a simple brunch of egg sandwiches and cream cheese bagels with English tea fulfilling a minimum $10 order per person and rightly so. Thoroughly enjoyed lunch followed by a sunny stroll up into Harlem afterwards for another iconic photo at Malcolm X Blvd. Happy days!

Love Seinfeld. Was happy to get in. The wings were too fried, like when the breading is all you bite and the rest is just too oily. No sauce either?
The gyro wrap was actually awesome. Warm throughout entire sandwich and a healthy dose of tzaziki sauce. Fries were crispy.
Still reasonably priced in NYC

Actually some of the best service I've gotten at a restaurant in the city and prices were cheap. One of those places where you get 1 chocolate milkshake and you end up filling that glass from the metal cup 3 times. Fantastic. Good gyro, didnt skimp on the lamb.

My family and I have been here on multiple occasions but I was there last week with my son for an early morning breakfast after a red eye flight from LA. The staff is so freakin’ friendly and welcoming. Food didn’t disappoint and we got to unexpectedly meet a person (famous) whom I’d like to keep a secret for their sake. Anyhow we’ll be back soon since we frequent nyc.

Visited while on a “blind book date” with myself. Waiter was so friendly, he highly recommended the milkshake! Which I thoroughly enjoyed, along with my fries.
Funnily enough I had no idea it was the restaurant from Seinfeld until I started watching it recently! I always wanted to read a book in a diner late at night and to think it was on a sitcom!!

Also, book store just around the corner on 112th, also recommend 😊

If you’ve seen the sitcom Seinfeld, then you know Tom’s Restaurant—the iconic exterior featured as the gang’s favorite hangout spot. But let me ask you, have you tasted the burgers? They’re as classic as the diner itself! Juicy, flavorful, and always satisfying, the burgers pair perfectly with their crispy fries. This is a place where you can eat, chill out, and enjoy the vibe.

Tom’s isn’t just a diner; it’s a community hub. Located in the heart of Columbia University's neighborhood, it has a unique vibe where the chatter of bright young minds fills the air (though not all of them are comedians—looking at you, Jeff Putterman, SIPA '93…inside joke, but unfortunately accurate).

Whenever I need to satisfy my burger and fry cravings, this is the place I turn to. The staff is always courteous, the service is prompt, and the food is consistently good. It’s the quintessential college diner experience that somehow remains timeless, even as the years—and my grey hairs—roll on.

Be sure to check out the attached picture and take a look at their extensive menu. Whether you’re in the mood for a classic burger, an all-day breakfast, or one of their delicious milkshakes, Tom’s has something for everyone. Trust me, you need to drop by and experience it for yourself. Come for the nostalgia, stay for the comfort food, and leave with a full stomach and a smile. Enjoy!
The Jerry Seinfeld’s restaurant, a classic place to visit in New York. The food was delicious and the waitress was kind and helpfull. Great experience.

I didn't read the reviews before traveling all the way to this place but I was excited to see it. We went in and was sat at a table. Staff was very busy talking to each other and pretending to be playing basketball which was very strange. The place was sort of run down especially the bathroom. My boyfriend ordered the kabobs and asked about what the veggies were that came with it. We were told assorted veggies. He loves veggies well he got veggies from a can not fresh vegetables. Really! $23 dollars for several pieces of meat, tons of rice and tons of vegetables from a can. If we knew this we would have just ordered a burger. I ordered the parm and cheese sandwich it was just okay. I only ate half of it. We were pretty disapppointed! We took a few pictures which was nice but wished we would have ate somewhere else and just maybe had a dessert here to see the place. Not what we hope it would be for the travel from Manhattan.
Seinfeld craz is long past gone. Now it's just a diner st the corner. Where you can wait at the counter for a man to pour your coffee

Just like anyone else who has seen Seinfeld, had to visit Tom's whilst in America.
Was there for breakfast and plenty of space available. It wasn't over top Seinfeld which I appreciated with small homages to the show.
Ordered the lumberjack (bacon, eggs and sausage), and a bacon and egg sandwich.
Food was okay for the price, felt it was a little expensive for the amount of food offered.
However the service was horrible, with the waiter barely looking up from his sombre.
Guy was pretty rude Very aggressive, then again most people here are but still. The plate of food was pretty bad, needed seasoning. Its alright food, more for vibes.

Big Seinfeld fan and while visiting NY my daughter surprised me with a trip to Tom's. Food was okay, my omlette was dry. But not bad, just not great. Service was good and the place was bustling. Great to actually see it.
Remember, each person must order a minimum of $12.

media.caption: Diner breakfast eggs hash browns bacon

reviews.snippet: As someone who grew up watching Seinfeld, I was really geeked to be able to see to this cafe in person. It really felt nostalgic, as watching the show was such a big part of my childhood.

Wanted to try this place because Seinfeld made it seem so surreal. I decided on ordering the fish and chips. To my disappointment, I was served fish fillet on a bun, which, in reality, is a fish sandwich. Even if I did order a fish sandwich, the fillet was slapped onto a cold, non-buttered bun. I might as well have ordered the fish sandwich from McDonald's and would have gotten my money's worth. On top of that, my friend's cole slaw was just dried lettuce. Service was friendly, but pretty slow. But the food? Mediocre at best.

Beautiful place, cheery staff, delicious food, good prices.
A must visit for Seinfeld fans.
10/10 Pancakes were puffy !
I had the chicken parm sandwich and it was great.
Constantin was really helpfull and even took some photos for us, Thank You !

One of the cooler diner experiences in NYC, the nearest from Colombia University. Expect it to be busy at most times, as it's flooded with students and locals. The food was great, the service was very fast and friendly, and is a must-go for a Seinfeld fan!
Good dinner service - top shelf french fries

We did all the fun tourist things and this was great, we love Seinfeld so this was a must stop. Food was great and our server at the bar was soo much fun, he made the trip worth it. The food was great and the prices were too.

If you're a Seinfeld fan they have super cool memorabilia all around! If you like good food and portions, they've got you covered too! Ordered the Gyro Sandwich and it was great! Really wonderful staff, they know what you need before you even have a chance to ask. Definitely recommend!

Listen, you don't come here for out-of-this-world food, or an incredibly elegant ambiance - you come here because you want an authentic, New York City-style diner experience. And in that respect, Tom's delivers. A Columbia University staple (and, of course, made popular by Seinfeld, the television show), you’ll find anything and everything you would in an NYC diner: sandwiches, pancakes, burgers, omelettes, soups, salads, pies, etc, etc.

Tom’s was a letdown. The burger felt lifeless, the bacon was basically fossilized, and I felt sick after eating. Larry David would’ve walked out mid-bite. Seinfeld nostalgia can only carry a place so far.
In NYC for a simple day trip and had to see this place. Cheeseburger was great and the atmosphere was perfect. Beautiful day with beautiful food.

Fast and great service. A must stop for Seinfeld fans. I didn’t get the big salad…
I had a cup of coffee, and hot pastrami sandwich.

Greeted at the door by cheerful staff, food was made quickly and everything tasted as expected. Staff were friendly and professional.

Very typical diner food with a iconic tv past.

Inside is cozy. There is Bathroom in the back but very small.

Seinfeld Fans, Tom’s is definitely a big slice of TV nostalgia! It’s neon Exterior graced almost every episode and even though the interior shots were filmed at a studio in LA. This spot is definitely a must see.

So stop it and grab a coffee, big salad or tuna salad sandwich and enjoy the walls filled with memorabilia! *Note the staff is very used to fans coming to the spot so feel free to snap a selfie or two with the signed pictures of the cast or the Kramer portrait while you chat with fellow fans visiting from around the world. *I spoke with a fan who traveled from Germany 🇩🇪

You probably should pick some other place if you're not a Seinfeld fan because that's obviously the main catch here.

The burger was the worst I've had here among over 15 other places. Dry and tasteless.

The staff was friendly, the food came fast and it wasn't expensive.

Level your expectations and Tom is an enjoyable Seinfeld-experience. Too bad the interiors aren't the same with the show!

This is more of a tourist attraction - the food is just average. The poor hygiene levels are difficult to ignore as sandwiches are prepared after handling money and dirty dishes. Nice to see once but I will not be back.

reviews.snippet: Great experience at the authentic diner. Food is excellent service even better!

Very upbeat vibe, great food, friendly, attentive staff. My kids took me there for my birthday because yes, I'm a Seinfeld fan. I stood in front of the iconic blue sign and it felt magical! Indescribable! I'll be back!. Also, I just read Entrances and Exits... highly recommend!

The facade as seen on Seinfeld. Some Seinfeld memorabilia inside and worth wandering over if you area fan.

Had dessert. Excellent rice pudding and huge milkshakes and malts.

Came for brunch on a weekday, there was no line to get in. Food was ok, but here you’re really paying for the nostalgia. One thing I noticed and disliked was that the waiter filled up one of our water cups too much and dumped the excess back into the pitcher which was then used to serve other tables. This is unhygienic! Went once for the memories but would not come back.

Food was very mediocre, only place in America where you get only one refill for soda. The menu said that with sandwich the cup of soup would be an extra buck, I was charged full price, I didn't want to make a fuss about it but I would never return.
It's a place that's living off being the exterior of a diner in a 20 year old TV series and it shows.

The service was good though, very nice waitress.
Fast and delicious breakfast. This place always hits the spot. It’s a little cool in there because of the overhead fans.

media.caption: Two eggs over easy with bacon and potatoes

reviews.snippet: Server took a $100 bill from us then lied and said we only gave a $50 bill… The manager was no help in the situation so we ended up paying $100 for a $40 bill. Criminal.
Yes this a must for Seinfeld fans! Food is average but the ambiance is great. Staff is also accommodating, fast and efficient.
Nice place, but I’ve had better burgers. It was juicy, it looked nice, and all, but I expected more. The fries were just okay as well. Service is very nice though, and does have some history.
Nice friendly staff, food is good, especially the green salad that comes with entrees. Prices are reasonable. It’s worth a visit if you are in the neighborhood.
Great apple pie with vanilla ice cream, and rice pudding! Staff was kind, great humor too 😉

The food was reasonably priced with good portion! The pancakes and egg benny both were not disappointed.
I love their retro vibe too :)
Food came out quite fast and delicious!! I had french toast with sunny side up eggs and coffee. I love this coffee too :)

If you love the TV show Seinfeld you have to come to this diner. If you don't know who Seinfeld is you still have to visit this diner. It's a traditional american restaurant with nice food and friendly staff. Highly recommended

doesn't feel like a tourist trap, but has some of the pictures of the cast members of seinfeld on the walls! food was good and not overpriced and the service was extremely efficient :) they don't sell merchandise here so if you go take some pics but not much else
Been coming here for over 20 years. Great food. Staff is great. Diner experience is good. They have newspapers that you can read for free. Always busy.
The food was soo good and there’s tons of Seinfeld merch on the wall it’s really cool

Ordered queso as an appetizer, which came out cold. Took forever to flag the waitress down and let her know. Appetizer ended up coming out with the food. The sodas were very flat. Also took a while to get that replaced. Ordered the Nashville hot chicken, was served the original chicken, but did not say anything about this, as we had already been waiting a while. The food was underwhelming. The waitress was not very attentive. There was a table beside us who’s order was wrong, as well. Probably will not be back.

In addition to being "famous" for being the Seinfeld Diner, Tom's is...a diner - it might say restaurant - but it is a booth diner. We had a groupon but even without it our food was incredibly reasonable. Our server gave us good advice on what to get and when one of our choices wasn't available they comp'ed the starter (that didn't come with the new choice). Fair. It felt homey and friendly. We were there in the evening on a Monday.
Picture - open faced Ruben - it didn't have the mile of meat at some other places, but, frankly - this was more to my liking.
Went twice with my daughter. They used this place's exterior for a scene from *Seinfeld* and they had good food.
The "Seinfeld" diner!! Delicious, lightning fast service...our food arrived before our drinks! Would definitely go there again.

The food is delicious, the staff are super friendly and it’s relatively cheap! You get a lot of food for your buck. It’s super cool to say you’ve eaten there. Lots of Seinfeld decorations and celebrity photos of who’ve eaten there.

I arrived there for the cultural importance (Seinfeld and Suzanne Vega) and its history, and decided to sit and have coffee while I'm there.
The place feels somewhat run-down, for example the "out of order" signs on the functioning bathrooms and the state of the cutlery.
Coffee was ok, unfortunately I wasn't offered a refill.
Service was ok; while sitting the waitress was nice, but when I received the check at the table, only after waiting 10 mins I was told I'm supposed to pay at the counter.
It's nice to check it out but I wouldn't bother to order something there.

Delicious food (...and they serve breakfast aaall daaaay looong)! EXCELLENT service, very friendly staff, and quick turnaround! Affordable! And....needless to say, the Seinfeld memorabilia add to the charm, and the Seinfeld exterior is a huge plus. We love this place!

We came here because my husband is a Seinfeld fan and wanted to visit while we were in the city. That said, I don’t watch the show often so the diner had no nostalgic charm for me. Nonetheless, it had a cool classic hole-in-the-roof vibe. However neither of us was impressed with the food. I got an egg salad sandwich and it was bland & dry. Unless you’re going for the Seinfeld connection, I’d say probably not worth going out of your way to visit.

Tom's Restaurant, located at 2880 Broadway in Morningside Heights, New York City, is an iconic diner famous for its appearance in the hit TV show "Seinfeld," where it doubled as Monk's Cafe. This unassuming corner diner has been a staple of the neighborhood since the 1940s, serving Columbia students and locals alike with its classic diner fare and cozy, nostalgic atmosphere .

For "Seinfeld" fans, visiting Tom's Restaurant is a delightful pilgrimage. While the interior shots for the show were filmed on a set, the exterior of Tom's became one of the most recognizable TV locations. Stepping inside, you won't find Seinfeld-themed dishes, but you will experience a quintessential New York diner ambiance with high-backed vinyl booths, a no-nonsense staff, and a menu that covers all the diner classics .

Even if you don't stop to eat, the experience of visiting Tom's Restaurant is worthwhile for the nostalgia alone. The exterior is perfect for those quintessential "Seinfeld" photo ops, and the inside feels like stepping back into TV history. The diner maintains its charm with a menu offering everything from hearty breakfasts to late-night snacks, all served with endless coffee refills .

Overall, Tom's Restaurant is more than just a spot for a meal—it's a slice of pop culture history that continues to draw fans from around the world. Whether you're a die-hard "Seinfeld" fan or just in the mood for a classic diner experience, Tom's offers a unique taste of New York City's rich cultural tapestry.
Was here because I'm a huge Seinfeld fan, made some time during my 3 day stay at NYC. Waiter was very responsive, friendly, brought my order in surprisingly quickly. Food was just ok.
Did not disappoint. Great burger, super friendly staff, awesome Seinfeld memorabilia, beautiful neighborhood. No AC, but overall comfortable.

You get the classic american diner experience here. Prices are friendly despite the Seinfeld fame, and there were no tourist group gatherings outside. Reasonably quick service even at the busiest of times.

Points off for the restrooms, which seem to be “momentarily out of order” - permanently.
If you’re a Seinfeld’s fan, then this restaurant is a must while visiting NYC. The food portion was small though.

Food is just an ordinary diner.
The staff were very nice and friendly.

This is worth visiting if you're a Seinfeld fan. But it's also a decent diner in its own right.

We enjoyed a hot pastrami sandwich and cheese and ham toastie, and they both hit the spot.
Ordered turkey club with bacon and cole and let me tell you how great it tasted. I can tell you that after I was done with I didnt feel bloated one bit and that equals no presevatives!!! Great job

I loved Seinfeld, watching still after many years. This cafe was the one depicted in the show, but was called Monks Restaurant (actually said Monks Cafe on the window in the show but had the still-there "restaurant" letters on the outside) Anyways, really busy all the time but decent food and stellar service.

As a Seinfeld fan I was excited to come here the food was decent not bad love the sausages yet the rest could be a bit better to be honest plus one of the waitress was being very rude towards my husband, gave Us menu's with grease on it when we told her it seem she didn't care, knocking on the bathroom door trying to open looking inside while he was in there knowing the customer sitting in front of Us who asked about the bathrooms because there was out of order signs saw my husband go in so of course she does that, also telling other customers including us to move while we're waiting on line to pay our bill and getting the food order wrong... Heh what a character she is. 😒
As the iconic seinfeld diner, my wife and I were pleased to have brunch here. Service was friendly and food was good.
It’s from the TV show Seinfeld, but even if it wasn’t, the food is great and well-priced. Really recommend!
Super friendly and attentive service! The food was pretty good. It's sort of typical diner fare. The French fries were amazing though. Just perfectly salted and crispy and fresh.
a good classic american diner! we were seated quickly and service was great.

Stop in looking forward to a nice Diner breakfast, I was told there wasn’t anymore booth available when I walked in but a couple had got up from the booth and left I asked the unprofessional Quote unquote Manager can I sit at the booth, with the loudest meanest voice he said “NO” and walked away, the customer be side me looked at me than said to him, so you’re the owner, he said yeah why, the customer began talking about Seinfeld and once again he walked away. This manager with a nasty attitude, really should be in the back counting numbers, he has the slightest idea how to be kind and respectful to the people that keeps this restaurant running. So whom ever is the actual owner of this restaurant, come and check in every now and then because I left without eating, I don’t have to take that from no one, and reading some of these reviews, and this place has left a bad taste in a few people’s mouths.

Such a disappointment. I came here with a group for the novelty of it being associated with Seinfeld. I was expecting a mediocre breakfast - we were paying for the experience. How bad can it be to ruin the experience. Well the food was that bad. Breakfast is so easy. Even mediocre does the job. This place was less than mediocre. 3 stars because it’s still iconic.

reviews.snippet: Tried Ethiopian food for the first time here and was blown away. I was in town and wanted to see the Jazz performance of Julia Danielle (amazing btw highly recommend) and met some friends for a nice, relaxed Sunday evening. We got a mix of sambusas which I highly recommend. They were so good and always brought out fast. The main dishes took more time, but were amazing. We shared a mix of food. The bread was so spongy and perfect for the mix of flavors. Injera is a must while here!

Five stars! This was my first time trying Ethiopian food and Massawa did not disappoint. I ordered the veggie combo and it was so, so good. Everything was flavorful, well seasoned, and such a fun first experience with Ethiopian cuisine. I also tried the sambusas (the little meat pies!) and they were delicious too, a perfect starter. The prices were actually really reasonable, especially for New York. The only thing I’d mention is parking can be tough, but honestly that’s pretty standard for a busy NYC area, so not really a negative. I’d definitely come back. Actually planning my next trip now 😂

Wonderful East African restaurant serving Eritrean & Ethiopian fare. The space and the staff are warm and inviting. I had a hot cup of cinnamon coffee while I waited on the rest of my party to arrive, I recommend it. Laid back cozy vibe, with space to chill while waiting for your table. We had lunch and the prices were great, and the portions generous. We had samplings of the vegan and vegetarian offerings, they offer different levels of spice and their were five in our group with everyone stated and happy. One person in our group also had salmon and attested to its tastiness, it certainly looked like it was prepared perfectly. The injera was light and had the perfect balance of tang - again, ample portions too. Swollen and happy, we had to decline dessert. Overall a wonderful experience. Great for groups, friends, kids, or an intimate date - soooo good!

Very friendly service. Food was delicious with a twist of no utensils. We started with the Sambusa Duo followed by the Fitfit Tebesi and Zegeni with injera. Both delicious with the spicier Zegeni. Great experience.

MASSAWA is an Ethiopian restaurant located in Harlem. It is a casual upscale restaurant, modern and elegant without being pretentious. The food and drinks were amazing! The cocktails were great. We had a MANGOTINI and a BUBBLE GUM MARTINI. For food, we had the vegetable platter which allowed us to try a whole host of things. We added a protein to that , a spicy beef stew. Everyone has a fun tome eating in this unique way. The minor pet peeves I had was that the waitresses didn't explain each dish, and the beautiful and clean toilet had problems flushing. All in all, a very fun, satisfying and unique dining experience.

Stumbled in on a rainy day after a long bus ride and were met with such exquisite hospitality and absolutely delicious food that I had to write a review. Everything is or can be gluten free and the atmosphere is so gorgeous and relaxing. We tried the honey wine on a whim and it’s superb. Marvelous experience, highly recommend to anyone, celiac or not, but being able to order anything off the menu was a particular treat for me.

This was an excellent place to celebrate a special occasion. The staff went above and beyond to ensure we had a wonderful evening. The dishes were prepared with fresh ingredients and presented beautifully. Every flavor was perfectly balanced, and the portions were generous. I would definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone.

The food was absolutely divine! Every dish, from the starter to the entree and the dessert, was simply amazing. It was the best I’ve ever had in the city. You can truly feel the love and passion that went into creating each dish. The atmosphere is incredibly lovely, and the staff is incredibly friendly and welcoming. I highly recommend this place!

One of the best restaurants we’ve been in NYC, very highly recommended. We didn’t have a reservation, but they were able to accommodate our group of 5. The food from starters, to main dish, to dessert were excellent! You can tell that the food was prepared with care and affection. The best way to enjoy their food is to order different things and share with everyone, including their desserts which were hard to pick a favorite. The ambiance is also great, we didn’t have to shout!

After hearing great things about Massawa from a dear friend for years, I decided to give it a shot. Last Friday, the two of us shared a trio of sambusas and an Alitcha Beghe entrée. Everything was delicious! We even had to order another pair of fish sambusas, as that was our favorite of the trio. All of the food is 10/10 though we never received napkins, a must when eating injera with your hands.
Our server was kind and pleasant, but slow and inattentive. She did not give her name, but volunteered her young teen age when we asked for drink recommendations. I received the tasty agave ginger lemonade, instead of the alcohol-based ginger lemonade I ordered. When I did get it, it was pure completely unpalatable. After dinner, we ordered pumpkin lattes with oatmilk. After 20 minutes of waiting, our server returned to tell us that the bartender left to buy oatmilk from a local store and scurried off before we could cancel. It took about 40 minutes to receive lukewarm lattes.
My friend loves this place and wanted to share it with me. The food was wonderful, but the service dampened the experience.

I have been frequenting this restaurant for over 35 years, and it never disappoints. While prices have gotten steeper and portions smaller following renovations that doubled the square footage and lent the previously unassuming space a trendier, more upscale vibe, Massawa remains the best Ethiopian eats in Manhattan. Additionally, the hosts are very gracious, and always ensure patrons—particularly habitues—are treated like family. Insider tip: The owners lived in Naples, Italy, for a long time, so the espresso and coffee drinks are out of this world.

I’ve been to several Ethiopian restaurants before, and this one is great. The menu offers a wide variety of options, including some more unique dishes you don’t often come across, like fish.

I’m a big fan of their slow-cooked chicken; it’s rich, flavorful, and clearly made with care. But what really surprised me was the dessert. I ordered the limoncello sorbet, and it was absolutely to die for. I wasn’t expecting such an explosive burst of flavor… it was refreshing, vibrant, and perfectly balanced.

I already can’t wait to go back just to have it again!

I came here for a Sunday night, dinner and really enjoyed the food. For our first experience of Ethiopian food, I enjoyed the flavors of my salmon dish and the red lentils. Ingera bread was tasty and something different. The Samusa was really good, but I did not care for the sauces. My Agave ginger lemonade drink was ok.

Very delicious Ethiopian food. We were a group of four, including one vegetarian. The very nice server recommended the goat stew and roasted chicken dish, along with the vegan sampler. This allowed us to try many of the top flavors. It was all delicious. Would recommend to all looking to have a fun experience with Ethiopian food.

response.snippet: Thank you so much for coming and sharing your experience! We’re happy to hear you enjoyed our traditional dishes. We truly appreciate your recommendation and look forward to welcoming you and your group again soon! ✨

reviews.snippet:
the restaurant is SO CUTE. would be good for dinner dates. each table has each flowers and the dotted floral decorations to well with the woody feel of the atmosphere. so worth coming by if you’re in the neighborhood.

the food overall was rlly good. i particularly enjoyed the samosa (2 sauces were very flavorful) and the garden salad (the dressing is light and goes perfectly balanced with the watermelon blocks and arugula). the ginger coffee was interesting and very strong.
