reviews.snippet: If you like Ethiopian food this is the place to go. Food is divine. Good cocktails too. Go before 7 for $9 specialty cocktails. The meat and vegetarian combos were both excellent. The Fava bean dip is divine.

The food was delicious!!! So so good. But the service was truly terrible. Maybe it was just the day we went, but multiple tables were getting up to leave after just getting a drink because the service was so slow.

We got drinks after 45 minutes, and they were wrong (and we still got charged). Then, our food came another 30 minutes later and was promptly whisked away because it wasn’t on the GF injera we ordered. The waitress was sassy to us the whole time, which would have been charming and funny if the service wasn’t terrible.

I really hope this spot can figure out the service because the food is 10/10!

Such a lovely place with tasty food! Has an outdoor protected from the wind area and quite large indoor space. We ordered a vegetarian sampler with lamb and salmon and it was way enough for two people. We could not finish the food but it was so good, especially spicy lamb! We also tried a rum cake which was just ok but then i do not have a sweet tooth so perhaps sweet lovers would appreciate it more. I have to say that the menu has many drinks options ranging from mimosas (for those who like festive brunches) to different teas and coffees. I highly recommend this great food stop and will be back myself for sure!

Food 5/5. Everything was flavorful and big portions. The space is nice and good for a date night or a bigger group. -1 star as some of the items on the paper menu were not on the digital ordering menu but our waitress was great and helped remedy.

Nice restaurant, food delicious - the items we ordered were actually similar to (home cooked) Indian - but less spicy - especially the lentil dishes and the Sambusa (similar to an Indian Samosa).

Lovely drinks - especially the Honey wine and the cocktails we ordered were decent too (see the picture of the receipt for the details).

Only feedback would be:

1. The Chicken and Veg Sambusa - we are existing mixed Sambusa (instead of one chicken one and one vegetable one - if we knew we have just ordered the chicken ones.

2. The Veg sampler was delicious but we felt a little pricy for the amount of food.

Very delicious and affordable Ethiopian cuisine.

We went in as a group of 4 for the lunch special and food was delicious. We had the spicy beef and the spicy lamb with collared green, potato stew, cabbage, chickpeas, and red lentils for sharing. You have the option to have individual plate or sharing a plate.

The fermented injera is fluffy like steamed rice cake and with a bit sharp sourness to cut through all the spices to balance the taste.

I think our favorites are spicy beef and chickpea. I ordered ginger coffee, which was quiet unique.

Also an highlight: the rum raisin cake is very very very strong in rum. It is a huge piece soaked in rum and alcohol lingers on the back if the tongue. It is very delicious but I won’t eat it if I needed to work in the afternoon.

Service is a bit slow. You scan QR code for ordering and for paying. Price is very affordable for what you get. It is on the side of Columbia campus and it is one of the best Ethiopian places to eat in the city.
I used to eat here during my Columbia years. Happy to be back. Lots of elbow room to try the food you eat with your hands.

response.snippet: Thank you, Sree, for coming back to Massawa! We’re so glad to welcome you again and honored to be part of your Columbia memories. Thank you for the wonderful pictures, too! We hope to see you again soon 💛

reviews.snippet: Incredible Ethiopian food in a beautiful restaurant. If gluten free make sure to ask for the pure teff injera - soooo good. We had the vegan sampler, ful (fava beans) and spicy lentils, as well as spicy tea, coffee and rum cake. Everything was delicious and enough for 3 people. So many vegan options!

I went to Massawa three times and every time, I had a terrible experience. Food is okay but far cry from some really great Ethiopian places. The worst thing is service – two out of the three times, we had to wait more than one hour to get our food, even though once the restaurant was almost empty and the other time, we saw other groups get their meals ahead of us despite arriving later. The meals are served as the staff wishes to serve it, not as it was ordered – we ordered two veg platters and one portion of meat separately. The food arrived all on one big plate – we didn't ask for it. Some people prefer to have their own plate or don't want to mix their food with meat. On top of this, one time the server added two dishes to the bill worth $40 even though we didn't order them. Eventually they were removed but it took as 20 minutes of arguing and escalating the issue to the manager.

The food was delicious! I would definitely return and recommend a visit to Massawa. My friend had the lamb, my son had the shrimp and I had the salmon. All came with with white rice and a potato dish that consisted of carrots and cabbage. My friend ordered okra with her meal which I sampled and enjoyed. I had chick peas with my dish, it was pureed and spicy by choice. I sampled my son's shrimp and decided if I return I will order that, not that the salmon isn't worth ordering again. The shrimp dish had a somewhat sweetness to it. The restaurant setting is nice and intimate. We ordered just after 3pm and was still within the lunch window. The three meals and two cups of tea cost $61.
Excellent food and service! Highly recommend the veggie platter

response.snippet: Thank you so much for the 5 star review Timaj! We love the picture, too and will repost it ✨ We’re so glad you enjoyed the food and service - and great choice with the veggie platter 🌱😊

reviews.snippet: Massawa is truly a 10/10 in every way ambiance, food and the service the staff here are incredibly kind, welcoming and genuinely passionate about what they do Every visit feels personal, like you’re being taken care of by people who truly want you to have a great experience. I always leave happy and already looking forward to coming back!

I love Ethiopian food and this spot does it great. It can be kind of a trek to get to this Morningside Heights spot if you don't live in the neighborhood, but this place is worth it.

The best way to enjoy your meal here is with shared plates on top of injera bread, which is how Ethiopian food is best eaten. If you're a party of two, I would recommend getting the vegan sampler and pairing it with a meat dish. The tebsi beef is my favorite, but the other options are good too. Pair it with a Habesha Ethiopian beer and you won't be disappointed.
I never tried Ethiopian food until my girl put me on a few weeks ago. This food slaps my taste buds around in so many ways lol. It’s a unique cuisine and I would def recommend trying it.

My friends and I went there for drinks. They have a decent selections of cocktails. We got the African rose, Bellini, and Mangotini which didn’t disappoint. 🥂great service and atmosphere. Plus, you can order and pay on your phone!

I hate that stupid order & pay cube they have, it's like ordering door dash at a restaurant. It turned out to not be mandatory to use it but it took so long for a server to come by that it was unclear what we were supposed to do. Same deal for paying the bill

Good vibes here otherwise but food was kinda just normal

Lunch plate was a great price for a healthy portion of rice (or traditional bread), meat and two sides. The lamb was just right with a bit of spice that added a depth of flavor but was t overwhelming. I would definitely come back to try some of the other items, I was interested in the beef stew as well! Very cute decor and ambience, good for dates as well
Food and atmosphere was great and servers are very kind.

We have decided to quit going here because they stupidly change the amount of food you used to get. Just a joke portion of lentils and a small portion of meat is 28$ dollars. 🙃

I mean are you serious? They also charge you for an extra side at 7$

Dinning here became extremely overpriced. Sorry but not coming here never again!

The experience merits many repeat visits. The five-star limit can't express this quality. Workers here delivered outstanding attention additionally. They provide recently prepared food displayed skillfully. This place has become my favorite and could be yours.

response.snippet: Thank you so much, Lloyd! Your words mean the world to us and we're so happy the experience made such an impression. Our team works hard to create positive and memorable experiences, and knowing we’ve become your favorite place is the highest compliment. We look forward to welcoming you back again and again!

reviews.snippet: Fantastic food. This is my first time enjoying ethiopian food and I have to say, it was worth the wait. I really enjoyed eating with my hands! The protein plate to share was amazing. Definitely coming back.

Wonderful, well-spaced ambience with beautiful Ethiopian food. I was ambitious and had the Ethiopian iced coffee for dinner & did not regret it at all.

We chose all of their sides, and had both the chicken and veggie sambusas as a starter. Heavily recommend either or a combination of the two. Wonderfully lit at night and excellent service near closing time.

The atmosphere is beautiful and the wait staff are very nice. The 3 stars are only for atmosphere and wait staff. I have never had Ethiopian food before and I went here because of the reviews, but the food had no flavor at all. I was prepared to have an explosion of delicious flavors and was extremely disappointed and actually very shocked. It was honestly the most bland food I’ve eaten. The person that came with me had Ethiopian food before and told me she’ll take me some place else for the real experience. I ordered the chicken and she had the lamb.

My meal here left a positive impression. The informal setting and friendly faces make dining pleasant. The workers here really care about good service. My future plans definitely include more visits to Massawa. Best wishes for your dining adventure.

response.snippet: Thank you Do for your kind words! We’re delighted the atmosphere and service made your visit memorable. It means a lot to know Massawa left a lasting impression and we’re happy to have you back again soon ✨

reviews.snippet:
First, do you think this is worth $26 (without tax and tips)? Plus tax is $28.31, and this still doesn’t include tips yet…
Second, maybe they just like to take things slow or they don’t have enough waiters/waitresses, because the wait time is very long. It took me about 20 minutes to order my food and another 20 minutes to see my dishes (totaling around 40 minutes before I can actually eat)!
Third, maybe it’s just me, but that “bread like”thing is really sour.
Fourth, this restaurant is said to be a halal restaurant. However, they do sell alcoholic drinks. So, I don’t think this restaurant can be considered as halal.

Went on a first date here 2 years ago, and now we're married and had our first anniversary dinner here.

Hoping it's open for years to come so we can enjoy more anniversary dinners here.

response.snippet: Scott, this truly means so much to us ✨ Thank you! Being a part of your first date and now your anniversary is incredibly special, and we’re honored to be part of those memories. Wishing you both many more beautiful years together, and we look forward to celebrating many more anniversaries with you! ❤️

reviews.snippet: Excellent Ethiopian food, I found it to be very close to Indian cuisine. The use of spice in the food was good and the Injera (was like dosa) was tasty as well. Good ambience and friendly host. I hear that the restaurant has been there for over 30 years. Good going, that 👍😊
Nice clean place with very convenient ordering and payment through Toast; everything we tried was very good, but a little on a spicy side

media.caption: Zegeni (beef), Alitcha Beghe (lamb) with sides of shiro (split peas) and tsebhi hamli (collard greens)

reviews.snippet: Abraham is a remarkable host. Generous in his hospitality and warmth. The food is exceptional. A must stop every trip. Every offering is a banger! You must go again and again!

The food is bland and very expensive - especially compared to the fantastic alternatives nearby (Awaze and Abyssinia). It tastes like bland gentrified indian food - none of the intense flavourful spices you get elsewhere. Feels inauthentic. I guess it caters to gentrified tastebuds, but is definitely not my thing.

The food was delicious!
we had Silsi Derho, it was really good and Ethiopian coffee was on point. Sambousa was good as well.
I would definitely return and recommend a visit to Massawa.

Poor service, took forever to get water. Food had little to no explanation when served. Had to hunt down our server. Food was great but unfortunately would not return for this poor of service at this price point.
First time trying Ethiopian food and it was delicious. Only downside is that the wait time to receive the food and coffee we ordered was long.
We got the vegetarian sampler and it was great. Not maybe the most amazing Ethiopian food we have but it was good. Service was polite and prompt. Outdoor seating was nice.
Casual but chic ambience. Excellent food. #NYC #Manhattan

response.snippet: Thank you so much Wamuyu for the amazing review and beautiful pictures! 💛 Hope to see you again soon ✨

reviews.snippet: The food is delicious and the restaurant wasn't crowded. It's a really nice spot for lunch, dinner, hanging out with friends, or having a romantic date. It's not often that I come across Eritrean cuisine and I love it.

Craving Ethiopian cuisine or just curious what it looks like? Your spot: Massawa. I especially loved the Vegan sampler which has Injira (bread) along with 4 side dishes: potatoes, lentils, collard greens, and chickpea paste. Delicious! Go for the non-veg sampler if you are craving meat. You will like Ethiopian cuisine so much once you’ve had food at Massawa, you are bound to come again.

We ordered the spicy lamb and the non-spicy chicken to share. The sides and the Injera bread tasted great, and the place had a happy hour. The lady who served us said that the restaurant had been around for 35 years, and I can see why. The place is popular for good reason, and an excellent place to visit and enjoy a good meal.

The food was tasty but there was an issue with our order and we wound up waiting over an hour for our food to come out. I’ll come back because the food was good and hopefully the kitchen issue was just a fluke. I loved the chicken tebsi and wasn’t a huge fan of the salmon.
Wonderful and personal feeling. We got great recommendations from the servers in the 2 times we were there, and they’ve all been great! The split pea really stands out though!

Yummmm
Took the vegan sampler it was delicious. More then enough for 2 hungry people. Best Shiro I’ve had! The soup was also very tasty. Good service will probably come back

BEST ETHIOPIAN FOOD IN NYC!!!
I have tried to find a better place in the city and this one is still my favorite. The food quality is beyond exceptional and the injera has an amazing flavor. Service is incredible as well! Highly recommend!!

Fantastic place with a great outdoor and indoor seating. Great service and the food was good, we had the shrimp, chicken and lamb dishes. The injera is also very fresh and tasty. Don’t miss this gem if in the upper west side.

High quality and incredibly flavorful food. I was particularly impressed with their vegetarian and vegan meals. The freshness of their food was outstanding. It’s always a pleasure coming back to this place.

We ordered all three entrees chicken, lamb, and beef: Tsebhi Beghe, Derho Hiwas, and Zegeni. Among all, beef is my favorite entree, because it is well-cooked and very flavourful. The lamb was a bit undercooked. Great ambiance, perfect for a dinner date.

I did not have a good experience with ordering for delivery (through Uber eats). The food did not match what we ordered (they replaced duba with veg sampler). The food came 15 minutes later than estimated (~55min from order to delivery). And the portions are not worth the $26 per dish. (I'm assuming the portions are larger when you eat there.) The food was tasty enough.
Nice Jazz music, live!!!
Never got to try the food. Arrived on time and 45 minutes later I asked about the food, they had completely forgotten about the order yet never explained what happened.

Food was great, Service was bad.

One drink of two ordered came out right away, took 20 minutes or so for the second even after I went to the bar to inquire. We waited so long for a second round of drinks we cancelled them. I ordered meat platter for myself and a salmon dish for my boyfriend who doesn't eat red meat. 25 plus minutes after the meat platter arrived I asked about the salmon and was told it was on the meat platter which I did not appreciate.

Love this place.. As an Eritrean it’s one of my go to for takeout. We also celebrated my father‘s birthday there with the kids and the staff was super accommodating. They also had a jazz night with live music on Sunday very cool!
This is the only restaurant in the city I travel an hour to get to. Best food ever. Be patient with the wait time, the food is worth it.

response.snippet: Thank you so much for making the trip to dine with us! We truly appreciate it. Your patience means a lot, and we’re so glad you felt the food was worth it. We look forward to welcoming you back again soon! 💛

reviews.snippet:
First time eating Ethiopian food. The injera bread was filling. They look like crepes.

The chicken cubes had jalapenos which made them kind of spicy, but still good
Great food really enjoyed it we'll definitely come bsck. Highly recommend
The food was incredible—simple, well-executed, and delicious. Easily one of my favorite meals lately. Can’t wait to come back.

This is a wonderful little place! We loved the food here! The special shiro is a must try! The hostess was really nice and helpful. Their bar with a soccer world cup replica will be a nice place to watch the upcoming soccer world cup! Also their selection of African beers was pretty good. I'd recommend trying tusker, nice mild lager that goes well with the food!

Lunch rush extends well into afternoon at this busy eatery. I was especially impressed with their dessert quality. Employees notice subtle customer signals. Massawa impresses with its thoughtful little extras. Strong backing for this place.

response.snippet:
Thank you, Ana, for your kindness and thoughtful words!
We’re fortunate to have such a caring and professional team, and I’m so glad to hear you were well taken care of. We’re also happy you enjoyed the dessert! We look forward to welcoming you back soon ✨

reviews.snippet: Delicious and authentic food and the portions are reasonably priced and reasonably sized. Attracts a diverse clientele, not only students from the University. They have gluten free njara for a small extra price.

response.snippet: Thank you Saul for the 5 star review! We're so happy you enjoyed our traditional food and are very grateful for your support ✨✨✨

reviews.snippet: Reminded me why I absolutely love Ethiopian cusine. Also - I'm adding Habesha to my list of favorite beers.

Going to an exceptional Eritrean/Ethiopian restaurant with good friends is the best!
We split several dishes which by the way come with automatic injera refills. Also if you are of age 😉, try the Massawa hard lemonade!
Excellent and authentic Ethiopian food! Served on a large flat bread with small Flatbread to eat the food with. You may request a fork if the traditional way doesn't work for you.
Had the tebsi mild (which isn't spicy!) First time trying Ethiopian food - I didn't know to eat with my hands, but it was fun! Food was delightful :)
Was difficult as an Indian to taste but it was too subjective. It tasted exactly like an Indian food in a different look. Good service and reasonable price
Great restaurant with excellent service! The staff are so friendly and quick. The food was also really tasty. This is a great neighborhood joint that I’ll definitely go back to again.
One of the best place I ate in, in NYC. The food is fresh and tasty. And the prices are like not in New York.

response.snippet: Thank you so much Promocje! We really appreciate you noticing how fresh the food is. That’s something we take a lot of pride in every day. We’re so glad you enjoyed everything and found it tasty. Looking forward to welcoming you back again soon! 💛

reviews.snippet: My children and I had a wonderful Mother’s Day dinner here. The food is delicious, as if you’re eating a homemade meal and my Aperol Spritz was equally impressive. Excellent service, friendly staff, Mathilda, Gabby, and another server whose name I didn’t get were all so welcoming.and pleasant atmosphere. Highly recommend!
My first time eating Ethiopian. Amazing experience 😊 we cleaned the plate, definitely coming back and bringing friends and family.

I love their food. I also love a restaurant where you're able to hear yourself talk. The food does take time to cook, but who doesn't like their food fresh. While you wait, you can have tea or a drink. Appetizers if you like. The restaurant has a dim light setting. The Mgr is always on site. The waitress down to the host is very welcoming. I've been coming here since I was a kid. The food has always been amazing. The weekend is crowded, so reservations are a must.

I ordered the in-bone goat dish with collard greens (included). I also ordered a side of Alitcha. None of the food was cooked properly. The carrots in the Alitcha were not tender. The goat was still tough. The food was also not spicy enough. Skip this one and venture further into Harlem for Ethiopian food.

I loved it so much!! All the food was so delicious and it was probably the best Ethiopian food I’ve ever had! Everything comes on a massive platter of ethiopian pancake. I suggest the vegan sampler, the dahab Beghe, and the Zegeni

response.snippet: Thank you so much! We’re so happy you loved the food 💛 Everything we make comes from family-handed recipes. Hope to see you again soon for more good food!

reviews.snippet: We went there Sunday night, waited for a whole hour for our food but nothing came. The servers were chilling there and just chatting. I am super disappointed, never come to this restaurant.

I’ve been dining at Massawa’s since the 1990s. My husband and I loved the original restaurant (except the bathrooms). We were thrilled the place reopened after a long hiatus for renovations. Overall, the food is still very good — but portions are considerably smaller; the spiced tea is bland and barely tepid; and some prices are too high (a bottle of sparkling water is $7.50 and two tiny sambusa are $9). The atmosphere is nice but lacks the warmth of the old place. Service was also lacking, especially as we ordered through the app — which I do not recommend as we ended up having to mix our additional sides onto the injera tray. $120 for two was more than we expected to spend (no alcohol or dessert) but will go back as the food is well-prepared. We will just order differently.

Here’s the thing: the food is always tasty, the server was very polite; WE WAITED AN HOUR FOR THE FOOD. My father is visiting from out of town and we both had plans we had to get to. We ended up getting our food to go because we needed to leave by the time it came. So I’m very conflicted because I’ve had a great experience in the past. Again, the server was very nice about it and didn’t seem to have any control over the situation. I’m very hangry.
Mind if a white boy get a little spice in his life?????
Stumbled upon this place, delicious food especially the gluten free injera! We loved it.

response.snippet: Thank you, Susie, for stopping by and for the lovely review! We’re so happy you enjoyed the food. We’d love to welcome you back again soon 💛

reviews.snippet: This spot had unexpected character. The restaurant delivers consistently. Hospitable, warm, inviting, qualified. The food quality went past merely great. This spot balances all elements perfectly.

response.snippet: Thank you Shelley for your thoughtful feedback! We’re so glad you felt the warmth and enjoyed the food. It means a lot to know our efforts made such an impression and we look forward to welcoming you again soon! ✨

reviews.snippet: I’ve lived on this block for 10 years, I’ve been in this Massawa many times before they expanded, after they expanded, and at their Broadway location many times as well. My meal today was not at the level I’ve experienced in the past, in fact not even close. The salmon dish, which I’ve had over the years several times, is always very fishy (only at this location…never fishy at the Broadway location, strange!). The turmeric lamb is in a sauce that’s very bland and honestly not enough of it, the lamb is tender but very dry, and generally speaking the portions were really not good today…it’s just too little for the price. The lentils were undercooked and didn’t have good flavor, not near as flavorful as the Broadway location. I can’t explain it, I’m very sensitive to these differences, something isn’t right about the recipes here. Not to mention, I distinctly remember having to select two sides per entree and now they only do one. Why is that? Idk. This location needs to step it up because their other location on Broadway is MUCH better, by a significant amount. Service and atmosphere are still great here though.
Excellent Ethiopian halal. Beautiful venue, courteous staff. Everything was quality and delicious. My son’s first time having Ethiopian and loves it!

First time visiting and trying their food. Was super excited, the food didn't disappoint And the ginger lemonade was delicious. Service was not the best and it took time for someone to take our order, I approached them when we needed something.

As a Habesha person, I cannot overstate how deeply disappointing this experience was. I had been patiently waiting for my turn to order when I watched a staff member invite someone who arrived after me to order first. After waiting for over an hour—during which I saw multiple people who came in after me get served—I finally asked a staff member about my order. They went to the back and handed it to me without even an apology. No acknowledgment. No accountability. Just cold food that had clearly been sitting around, completely forgotten. Time is valuable, and this kind of service was not only disrespectful but incredibly inconvenient.

But what really makes this worse is the food. As an Ethiopian, I know what these dishes are supposed to taste like—and this wasn’t it. Not even close. I truly believe injera wasn’t made from authentic teff flour. It completely bland and missing the signature sour bitterness of true Ethiopian injera (which is unstable to any Ethiopian!!!!). The dish I ordered tasted like a watered-down, gentrified, whitewashed version of traditional Ethiopian food. The rich, distinct spices and flavors that define our cuisine were completely absent. It felt like an imitation made for people who’ve never had the real thing and wouldn’t know the difference.

Given the cost, the quality is downright insulting. I’m genuinely upset and cannot recommend this place to anyone. It’s a waste of money, the service was unacceptable, and the food simply sucks—trust me.
Doro wat was tender and spicy enough, made with the ferenji palate in mind. Perfect injera but don't be shy to ask for more on the side. Great service even on a busy night. This is the one.
Take out was great, fast delivery and not expensive, the 3 dish sampler is filling

Best ethubian food
Zegney great

Coffee wow macitto

What a magnificent restaurant! I love Ethiopian food. I tried once before and loved it, and I always wanted to try again. This place has wonderful Ethiopian food, smells great, and tastes yummy!Also, the survices should largely be highlighted. The staff there was so kind , courtesy, and professional! The food is one of the best I ve ever has for a while.

We've been going to this restaurant for over 20 years and it keeps getting better, if that's even a possibility! The food is delicious, portions are perfect for sharing and the environment is perfect for couples and families. My husband and I started going there when we were dating and we now go with our two kids. We all love it! We done in and take out too! Highly recommend it!
everything on the menu from the ginger agave lemonade to the amazing stews and lentils is delish -cannot go wrong. the use of berbere spice is just right. literally cleaned my plate

response.snippet: Thank you Billy for such a wonderful review! We’re so glad you enjoyed the ginger agave lemonade and the lentils. Hearing that you cleaned your plate is the best compliment we could receive 😊 We look forward to welcoming you again!

reviews.snippet: My daughter is a student nearby and this place quickly became our go-to spot when I come in for a visit. The food is so good! We love to get the vegan sampler for two. It's huge and we love every bite. The staff is warm and friendly and even when it's busy the food comes in a timely fashion. Highly recommend.

Wonderful experience in every way! Food was fantastic, service was just as good. We told our server that we were new to Ethiopian cuisine, and she could not have been kinder or more helpful in helping us navigate a cuisine new to us. We had beef, lamb, and chicken with various vegetables. It was all so good, it's hard to single out anything. It was all incredible. Great experience!
Excellent food and ambiance. Service a tad slow but was worth with the wait.

This place was nice inside but the food, which only started to arrive after an hour and 15 minutes, was not great. It was good, but for the price, you'd hope it was great. Nice cocktails.

The ordering system was obnoxious, there are no waitstaff, not really, just servers. The system worked well but I want a grub hub app experience at a sit down meal; give me a human.

Also a homeless guy came in and begged at every single table, there is is almost no staff there no one saw him. We'd have shared our food with him, ideally getting staff to bag something up, but we were in the middle of the hour wait for it.

Anyway, overall its fine. Don't need to go back. The places that are less fancy tend to be better food.
This place is a MUST! Great food, staff, and atmosphere! Highly recommend.

Two things really set this place apart. First, the unusual flexibility - I love how I can build my own veg sampler via the menu of side dishes. Second, the incredible flavors, richer and deeper than from nearby peers (Awash and Lalibela are also high quality but Massawa has the most interesting flavors). Friendly staff and strong packaging for takeout.
Injera is delicious! I love it

Went for lunch during the week and this place was PACKED, which is a testament to how delicious the food is and how nice the staff is. We got two chicken sambusas, a vegan platter for 2, and the spicy lamb for 3 adults and it was perfect. Mango margarita was also delicious.

The place is nice, but we were quite disappointed with the service. We arrived around 3:00 PM, and there were plenty of tables available. I specifically asked if we could sit inside or outside, and the young lady who received us said we could choose. We decided to sit inside.

Since we had just had lunch, we only wanted something to drink. The server didn't seem pleased but brought our drinks. She brought the check also, even before we were ready to leave. I had considered ordering additional items, but not after receiving the check so early.

When I was about to pay, I mentioned that I felt like we were being rushed out. She then explained that indoor service is more for dining. It would have been really helpful to know that when we arrived.

A friend recommended this place. The food was great! We had a vegan amongst us, so we ordered a vegan option to share, and it was delicious. Also cool experience scooping the ingredients with the bread. The music was great too. Very talented musicians. It was an unusual pairing of the cuisine and music but it was definitely fun and great experience. I would come back if I'm ever in NYC again.
The veg sampler was delicious and very filling!

WOW. The food here was INCREDIBLE. Next level. A little on the pricey side but worth it. Their ordering system seems chaotic, with online and in person ordering happening during dine in, but the food was worth it. A little wait because it was so busy and because of the aforementioned chaos, but still worth it. A totally unique dining experience, with food so good I'm glad my apartment is only half a block away, I'm going to fall into a happiness coma. The honey wine is also not to be missed. Leah the bartender apologized for the wait and was so kind she comped my 2nd glass of wine for the wait. Absolutely incredible service and the only competition was the food.

It's been almost a year since we went to Massawa but I'm still thinking about it. A lovely Ethiopian/Eritrean restaurant in the Upper West Side.
Food was hearty and super delicious. However, what I loved the most was the atmosphere and the interior design - modern yet rustic, a bit bare, very cozy with a hint of honey warmth (just like the honey wine we tried there). I'd love to return to Massawa one day.

Lovely atmosphere and great food! The service was excellent as well. Both the hostess and my waitress were helpful and sweet. I highly recommend the African Rose (light on the ginger) as an alcoholic beverage. It was delicious!

Love everything about this place. It is clean, organized, and the waitstaff are lovely. The food is definitely the best Ethiopian food in NYC. We got the lamb and beef meals and it was so delicious. Large portions too! Overall worth the price!
Delicious food. Had Shrimp Tebsi w/ Shiro for lunch. Carrot cake for dessert. Did not disappoint. Never does. Consistently delicious for years.

One of the best and most authentic East African/Ethiopian restaurants on Manhattan Island. Kind, welcoming, and attentive wait staff. A recent expansion has enabled installation of a small bar purveying imaginative, killer cocktails. For any occasion, order up a bottle of the great, imported Ethiopian honey wine. Way more subtle and flowered than meade and the perfect foil for all well-spiced dinner entrees. Great supplies of the soft, spongy bread (injera) typical of Ethiopian cuisine accompany all entrees. Superb and highly varied vegetarian and vegan options at all meal times. Great vegetable sampler platters perfect for sharing! Make this place one of your go-to destination feeds. (Can get super-busy and crowded evenings--always make a dinner reservation. Many walk-ins got turned away on our last Thursday and Saturday night visits.) Reserve and Go Already!

My wife and I had dinner here last night and enjoyed every minute of it. The menu offers vegan and non-vegan options, the food is plentiful and delicious - the non-alcoholic drink is delicious! Our waitress had a really great sense of humor. We made an evening of it - first walking around the neighborhood then walking West through the park, stopped to take some photos with a relaxed lady liberty, and headed over to dinner.

We thoroughly enjoyed a wonderful Ethiopian meal here. Even the wine and beer list were a pleasant surprise, with selections from Ethiopia and South Africa that were delightful. Some of the dishes were a little spicier than I usually tolerate, but so delicious that I could not stop eating them. Wonderful service, ambiance and food.

Excellent Ethiopian restaurant with great food and staff. Vegetarian and meat options depending on your preference, and all well seasoned. If you go for the combos, there are lots of options for different dishes to try. Injera was light, fluffy, and warm. Each of the entrees are well portioned and fresh. Service is quick and the staff are very kind. They have an outdoor patio/porch seating for when the weather is nice. Nice selection of Ethiopian beers. Overall, this place is delightful!

I had never tried Ethipoian cuisine b4 and was eegar to try it . I came here for lunch and was pleasantly surprised by the calming ambiance of the entire restaurant. Sever did great at explaining everything , and even made a suggestion for the Vegan sample platter...which I had +enjoyed throughly ! I plan on coming back soon for a date ...so I can try EVEN more food ...especially the dessert. I have not ONE complaint about this place ....10/10!

We used to come here at least once a month, loving the food and atmosphere. But this year they changed the menu to much smaller portions and they now only include 1 instead of 2 sides. Unfortunately, this changed it from an already expensive experience to a vastly overpriced one. The staff is friendly, but there is not really a service. You have to order yourself online, which has often lead to issues with the order due to an incomplete menu, and if you need the staffs assistance you wait forever.
We don't really want to come back here anymore and are very sad about it.

QR menu, which I personally struggle with. We ordered as a group on my friends phone, although the hostess was willing to take our order personally as they were not busy yet. The order got slightly confused and we got an appetizer (and charged for it). Food, drinks, and deserts were amazing. We feel amazing after. The rum cake is to die for.

The pro: the food was AMAZING! perfect combination of rich flavors and different textures.
The con: we did not have reservations so we had wait A LONG TIME to get served (the food prep time is not part of this although it did take a while). The other guests (assuming they had a reservation) were served promptly. I’d say it was a mistake on our end for not having reservations but still doesn’t warrant the long wait time for those who do not have reservations.

Overall: make a reservation when you go if you don’t want to wait ages but the food is worth it!
It took around 1 hour until we got our food.
Wonderful experience with Ethiopian food and coffee.
Ambient environment with decent plates for sharing. Automated payment with limited human service

This place is a unique experience. I have a friend that recommended this place because they have been coming here for years pre-pandemic. Sadly, they felt the customer interaction was leaking post-pandemic. We think the food is great because they have vegan and non-vegan options. It was really tasty. However the customer interaction was missing from my experience. This place is all cashless and there is no receptionist to seat you. You just grab an empty table and start ordering using the QVC codes on the table. This is an Ethiopian restaurant where it is customary to use your hand to eat. This was my first time experiencing Ethiopian dining. It would have been nice for someone to explain the system and the dishes before we ordered. I like that customers have to use their own phones to pay. Overall this place is cool it is just leaking some customer interaction for a first time customer.

We love Ethiopian cuisine and know the best in NYC is in Harlem. We brought our skeptical friend here to try this cuisine for the first time, and he loved it and enjoyed every dish.

We ordered a vegan and meat combo for two off menu, extra injera, and two beers for 3 adults. At first, we thought the portions were too small, but by the time we finished and the injera expanded in our stomachs, we realized it was the perfect amount of food.

You can dine indoors or outdoors. As it was a gorgeous day, I wish we dined outdoors. The interior is nice with a large bar. Typical design for most of these nyc Ethiopian restaurants. Our friend commented it was more spacious than Manhattan restaurants he's been to, but we find this typical of Harlem ones. It was his first time in this neighborhood.

The food was quite good, but not the best we've had in Harlem. Priced a bit higher than expected. Great drink menu, but $48 for a bottle of honey wine seemed excessive.

Staff was very friendly and pleasant, but as with most Ethiopian restaurants, it was a bit slow to respond to requests like for a menu or napkins despite few customers for late lunch around 3ish.
Excellent taste of Ethiopia, the best I have tasted in NYC. I definitely will be going back.

Really good Ethiopian food! The menu is a bit confusing, but one dish per person was plenty for dinner time. I don’t think we actually finished all of our food. Each dish comes with sides, so it becomes loaded quickly.

They also have an awesome happy hour with $6 cocktails. That alone makes me want to eat more Ethiopian 😀
Perfectly solid Ethiopian restaurant. I enjoyed the food but fairly standard overall

Great atmosphere, friendly service, and incredible food. We had the shrimp tebsi and vegan sampler and were very pleased. The shiro, timtimo, and shrimp in particular were excellent, but everything else was great as well. Prices are a little steep but as expected for New York.

For some reason when I went to this place I thought I was going to an Indian restaurant. Imagine the waiter's look when I asked her if they had lassie. She went from slightly amused to panic while politely explaining to me that was a drink you'd get at on Indian restaurant, not on an Ethiopian restaurant.
Food choice was varied enough to allow you to pick your favourite but not to extent to the point that you end up 10 minutes just to figure out what to eat.
Being an Ethiopian restaurant when the food arrived there was no cutlery. You eat by picking up discs of very thin flat brand and using it to pick up your food.
Everything is served on a giant platter from where you and all the people in your party will eat. It was great fun!
I was on a business trip and having lunch with a customer, it was a great way to break the ice and we all ended up having a laugh and dropping most of the useless formalities.

The food was delicious! And being served of the same platter I got to try several different dishes. It was quite filling as well. Not too spicy but definitely not bland, everything cooked to perfect tenderness.

This is a great place for casual lunch or dinner, especially if you bring some friends (or acquaintances) with you.

Service was fast and very pleasant.

The food was amazing. There was a very warm welcome from Abraham. We were there once 3 years ago and Abraham could still remember us. Every time we are in New York we love to go there at least once. Highly recommended for everyone.

Wanted to love this place after hearing good things. However we had a very disappointing experience. It took an hour for our appetizer to arrive. When I asked about this the server said there is normally at least a 45 min wait for food. That is not ok, especially since they don’t even bring any kind of snack or bread for the table. Appetizer was delicious but not worth getting hangry for an hour. The entree came an hour and 15 min after ordering—the people next to us who arrived after we did were already completely done with their meal. This is baffling since everything on the menu seems to be stews that just need serving. Such a shame.

Was raised eating this since I was a baby! I enjoy there zigany, bread and vegetables every chance we get to go there. We know the people who run it too and are like family as well, they are kind and funny people who do great service. Would recommend eating here when you get the chance and hope they never go out of business

The injera bread is very unique, the shared plate means you can get combination & the meat is halal which makes it even better. The meat was tender, the vege options were creative and it is a wholesome meal & a great coffee spot, too. I can see how it's a dynamic space; get coffee here, or get dinner here.

I’ve been coming to this place for about 15 years or so. I usually do take-out because I want to pig out in the privacy of my home. It can get a lil’ messy. It’s family owned and operated with friendly staff. I’m so thrilled that they’ve survived through the pandemic and quite surprised I’ve not left a review. The food is amazing and you have to try the honey wine. I’m looking forward to eating in again in their remodeled and expanded space.

I took family to a local Ethiopian restaurant Masawa on W. 121st St. for the first time in years. The owner was rude - speaking to every table but my table, the server was over whelmed. The owner helped other tables, mine was forgotten. Hostess tried but the service was poor, and food was bland. The music was a poor selection of top 40 hits; the bartender Mo was great. Moving forward, I will only go to the real Ethiopian restaurants whose culture and people are warm. To pay over $100, then treated less than deserving of a waitress check in; was poor customer service. I will not be going back - ever.

Very tasty food! Nice atmosphere!! Great lunch special prices !!! A's across the board ! I was sitting outside eating, drinking my honey wine when a tiny fly went into my drink. The waitress quickly exchanged my drink with no questions asked. Superb customer service !! Will be back again and again

Wodase was absolutely incredible (she made us the most delicious ginger lemonade) and it is such a pleasant atmosphere. I’m excited to try the shrimp which I ordered not too long ago but I have never had a bad experience here. Come check it out!
Delicious. My nephew suggested it. Said he loves it. So we loved it as well. Great service, music and food.

Best Ethiopian food in New York City, and if you’ve never tried Ethiopian cuisine before, give it a shot! You’ll discover a world of new textures, flavors and aromas.
**Lot of options for vegetarians and vegans **Samplers are great for sharing with friends. (Each main course dish can be converted into a sampler with the sides)
**All mains come with free/ extra injera (bread), so don’t worry about ordering more
**Their Ethiopian blend coffee cocktail is the best ever!!

Service is slower than what you expect in NYC because everyone is in a rush but I guess it’s partly because lot of the food is made fresh and partly because it’s their vibe :) they want you to relax and enjoy, not stress about eating out!

Small, simple and smooth spot. I can't believe that I have been in this area a few times without taking note of this beauty.

Lots of choices when it comes to alcoholic beverages from Ethiopia (I can't stand it when I go to a restaurant representing a country without any drinks from there.) Beer, wine, you name it I was impressed!

The prices were affordable, this is a good spot to bring a date if you leave nearby and you can also do groups of about 10 if I'm not mistaken.

Staff also deserve serious praise. You feel welcome as soon as you step in.

Completely over-priced and small portions. If you’re from a city with abundant Ethiopian restaurants like I am (Seattle), you may be disappointed with the food.

The cocktails were nice, though.

Nice wine from Uganda and great experience as you can see from the live jazz band and food.
Cozy atmosphere, great people and it is close to some campuses Making it very convenient spot for students and people from all walks of life. I will be frequenting this place for sure whenever I'm in town. Good job guys, keep it up!

Real simple decor with fantastic Ethiopian fare. I love really getting connected with my food and there’s no better way to do it than to dig in with your fingers. Great for groups and food sharing. Definitely the kind of food that brings people together.
Excellent Ethiopian food. Service was great too I tipped 30%

The decor was quite nice, warm, and cozy, and the food was very good (although know that you will eat with your hands). The only problem is that everything is well overpriced (as is commensurate with the neighborhood in which the restaurant is situated). I ate at a similar restaurant in a less expensive neighborhood; the food/service was just as good but the meals were half to three-quarters the cost. I will admit cost should be a variable judged extraneous to quality, but $8 for a bottled beer? Yes, I'm from out of town; I assume New Yorkers in Manhattan are use to being price-gouged.

Portions are atypically small for this type of cuisine. Food is lightly/barely spiced. Approaching bland. Wait staff not very attentive (especially near end of meal). Great to experience once, but certainly not a favorite. 1st and last visit. I'll look for another Ethiopian restaurant.

After eating one of the best meals in recent memory, (delicious, authentic food, friendly and helpful service, pleasant renovated interior) and certainly the best Ethiopian of all time, I realized much later, and after the restaurant closed) that I had left my phone on our table. The staff at Massawa couldn’t have been more helpful in safeguarding my phone and assuring me it would be able to be picked up the next day.
I am writing this review from said phone. Thank you Massawa!

I ordered an appetizer, Salad with Salmon for $15. Personally, it was big enough to be my entire meal. The Salmon was cooked well, seasoned nicely. Vegetables were fresh.

You order and pay for everything through your phone, even for dining in.

Ordered the vegan sampler for take out today and it was amazing! So much variety and a huge portion size. I especially loved the shiro and timtimo. Would definitely order here again or do dine in as the inside looked beautiful too!

We’ve been here a few times and the food has been consistently good. For lunch we had the chicken in berbere sauce which was our favorite and the lamb alicha, which is a bit milder. The lunch menu prices are reasonable for the quantity and conveniently located right across the Columbia campus. For dinner this past weekend we had the lamb tsebhi which was a thick stew cooked in berbere sauce and had a nice spicy zing to it. The honey wine works well if you find it too spicy.
Excellent food training waiter did not know what to do but tried interesting menu something for everyone
Incredible Ethiopian food and great staff...

I do not understand why people are so excite about this place. I came in around 4:15 pm to meet with a good friend of mine. Before a server took our order she sat down at a table next to us to have her lunch break or something. There was no one else on the floor, so I kept looking at her. She continued to chew her food and looked back at me. We sat at our table with menu open for about another 15 minutes watching the server having her lunch. Then another girl finally came up to us and took the order. I had an appetizer sampler platter for one - not worth ordering. The description in the menus sounds so much more delicious then the actual dishes are. Their famous special coffe is only served until early afternoon. I’m giving two stars for the vibe. It was cozy and quite. I will definitely not be coming back.

Spectacular! The food is incredible and the staff members are delightful. The best Ethiopian restaurant I've ever visited - the meats are so well prepared and presented. Go hungry! I highly recommend this restaurant!
Best Ethiopian food we have had hands down. Wonderful family owns and runs this warm, neighborhood anchor restaurant. Very consistent and enjoyable.

Three of us ordered two entrees and were thrilled -- and filled -- by a beautifully presented platter of delicious food as carefully presented as what you might find at a sushi restaurant. I would add a star if I could for the service -- so warm, welcoming, and helpful that I felt like a regular from the second we arrived. This place is a gem.

This place is the loveliest tastiest and friendliest out there. I studied nearby and would have the same meal maybe 3 or 4 times a week. After some time, they would even recognize my voice when I called to order something. Because of Massawa I discovered a world of new tasty things I didn't even know I liked. It is totally worth it to get out of your way, if necessary, to have a piece of Massawa goodness <3

AND they’re completely vegan friendly

Yummy! I love Ethiopian food and this is better than most of what I've had in Manhattan. I got the Massawa sampler and everything on it was delicious. They choose the side dishes for you, although you can say if you really want something in particular. Glad we did 't dictate, though, because they brought things I wouldn't necessarilly have chosen, but found delicious anyway, particularly the red lentils, which were absolutly incredible. I'm starting to think you can really judge an Ethiopian restaurant by their red lentils. These were excellent!

We ordered a family style platter with spicy chicken, lamb, pumpkin, lentil, chickpea, and stewed cabbage. It was amazing. The waiter was super friendly and even have us a complimentary dessert. We'll be back soon!

Absolutely the best restaurant in the area. Authentic Ethiopian and Eritrean cuisine. Inexpensive. Columbia students and faculty friendly. Discounted prices for lunch. Take reservations ahead of time. Large crowd friendly. Decent wine collection. Best African coffee in this area.

Pleasant, soothing ambiance; low noise level; food was flawless (and low on spice level); service was flawless too; they sell their spice blend if you'd like to bring it home. I found this place to be better than the other two Ethiopian eateries in midtown.

Literally some of the tastiest food I've ever eaten! The staff were so kind and the food was outstanding. My husband and I shared a plate and an appetizer and it was plenty for the two of us. I'll go back just for the bebere sauce!

Ordered delivery!
I thought the side dish portions left a bit to be desired, BUT the food was great! I don’t think I know enough about Ethiopian to comment on the details, but I was a fan and definitely will order or visit again!

Massawa used to be one of my favorite restaurants to go to with friends near campus; however, they recently reduced the amount of sides that come with an entree from 2 to 1. While this sounds like a minor inconvenience, it messes up the ratios of their meals and reduced the value of their lunches/dinners — as you are now receiving smaller meal servings for the same price. When asked how much it would be to purchase the (once included) second side, I was told this would cost $7. With this change in effect, purchasing Ethiopian food at the food truck parked outside of the Columbia gates (which has similar quality food and 2 sides) is far more practical than going to Massawa, as one could get two meals at the food truck for the same price as 1 smaller meal of similar quality at Massawa. My friends and I have decided to quit going to Massawa since this change, and we sadly don’t plant on going back anytime soon.

Great experience, fantastic food and people. Healthy and hearty, absolute must for Ethiopian cuisine lovers, and for all others open to new, interesting foods. We had vegan sambusa, vegan combination platter, tsebhi beghe, and two coffees. Everything was just yum!

I made a reservation for 8 and arrived on time. We were only checked in on twice in the first 30 minutes before they even took our order. It was a 7:30 on a Tuesday night so it was busy but we were very patient. I only got really frustrated as our food didn't come till after 9 PM! We were all so hungry we ate in 10 minutes. There was no communication about why our food was so late or how long it would be taking and there was nothing offered to us while we were waiting. We are college students and it was very difficult to have waited for so long without any reason why or any respect really! After trying to explain why it was a frustrating experience, we were met with defensiveness. I understand many places are understaffed and very busy, but I think there was a clear reason why we were not serviced at all and its because we are young, femme students.
Nice indoor and outdoor seating, great service and delicious food!!! Lots of vegan and vegetarian options!

Rich Ethiopian cuisine. Packaged for take-out in compartments, with teff separated so it doesn't get soggy on the way home. Friendly service; safe pick-up. We also ate outside there around November(?) on specially built level platforms (sidewalk is sloped) and had an equally enjoyable meal.
Great Ethiopian food but I prefer the vegan options

I am Eritrean and was craving some injera so I had to eat here. The food was pretty decent and definitely satisfied our craving. I was a bit thrown off by the fact that you don’t really interact much with the staff as you order and pay online. Kind of gave me fast food vibes. Maybe it has to do with Covid and what not. But overall I would definitely return and next time get the spiciest level. If you’re used to this food, the medium spice level was not spicy for us at all.

This is my second time at the restaurant. They were a little understaffed this time but they did a phenomenal job. The food is flavorful but spicy so be ready. Great atmosphere, food, and workers. Will continue to come here
This is the only Eritrean restaurant in New York City. It serves authentic diaspora cuisine that reminded my Eritrean wife of her childhood food. Can’t wait to go back!

response.snippet: Thank you so much Nicholas for your kind review! It means so much to us that our food brought back memories of home for your wife. We look forward to welcoming you again soon! ✨

reviews.snippet:
Love this restaurant! I usually have chicken tebsi or beef zegini, so my food experience from there is mostly based on these two dishes. The food is unbelievably tasty. Every bite is like “wow”. I often order for pickup and portions are really generous.

The interior of the restaurant is not fancy, but nice - imagine a place where college professors go for lunch, that would be the right description.

The only thing that I don’t like about this place is that they don’t deliver. I work 10 minutes walk from there and when I called once to order for delivery, the lady on the phone said they have to charge me $25 to deliver $13 lunch special meal. The guy that works there is very nice, so maybe had he answered the phone he would have been more accommodating. I never tried calling for delivery again.

Amazing food at an affordable price. I've had both the lamb and beef dishes here, and they are both fantastic. The bread as some have mentioned has an odd taste, but it seems to compliment the food when eaten together. They know what they are doing.

Nice people and location - but this is food is made for the western palette. No flavor at all but oh well i suppose they cater to the students. Tibsi is the easiest thing to make but yikes taste like nothing same with Shiro - needs garlic and tomato think they must just mix it with water and call it a day. Its not spiced enough. Food was better last time i went in 2009.

Renovated and more spacious than before. Pleasant atmosphere, with a more Ethiopian inspired decor than in the past, this is definitely a restaurant in which you will want to dine.

Portion size is reasonable and the spices are savory.

Decently good food, but the main problem was the service. The waitress was nice but very spacey. We had to ask for more water and we received and finished our entrée before our appetizer came out. We finally asked for them to cancel our order since they kept telling us the appetizer was "being made" when we had already finished dinner 15 minutes earlier.
Glad to have different option for dinner but the staff need to get it together

The food taste good but they serve you very small portions. My plate was covered with two sheets injera (bread) but only one was needed for the amount of food they gave me. I wouldn’t return back here. There are better options in Harlem.
$40 for one plate of food is just too much
I really love their coffee and Lentil Soup!

My favorite place for Ethiopian food in the city. Everything is so good here! My favorite is the lamb tibs and the okra dish they make. Great lunch deala. Just make sure you're prepared to come out smelling of spices when you leave the restaurant -- maybe don't make any fancy or sexy plans after dinner here. ;)

Food was excellent . Their injera is very fresh and juicy . I got the tebsi derho(seasoned chicken breasts with sautéed tomatoes berberé) and with a side of cablo (sautéed cabbage) and tsebhi hamli (collard greens cooked with mild spices ). The food was flavorful and gave me a taste of Ethiopia . Great margarita. I will be back !
Amazing service. Beautiful decor. Incredible coffee.

Tasty food, lovely spot, good vibe. Delicious ful and samosas that were really crisp and light with great sauces. My critique would be that it’s a little oricey and service was very friendly but not sharp.

I have never been to any restaurant that is consistently so good every single time. It is a great restaurant with many options for vegetarian diet. The staff is very warm and welcoming (except the bartender in evenings).

You order on a phone app thing but there is still table service. Sometimes the food takes a while to come out and sometimes the sides aren’t what you asked for. It’s still a great place though and the food is great and the people working there are great. You don’t always get what you ask for or on time, but just relax ok. Why are you in a rush. Just chill and it will come. Try it.
Delicious vegan sampler place, a bit over priced though.
It looks good but tastes not. My friend and I won't come here again.
One of ten average Ethiopian places. Definitely have had better more fresh Ethiopian food than this one.
OMG we visit from Texas I was nervous n skeptical but it was so delicious..if your every in NY give them a try and the service and hospitality is superb.
Have loved the Shiro and other food here for 30 years. One of the first if not the first, Ethiopian restaurant in NYC.

The food was flavorful. My favorite Ethiopian/Eritrean dish in general is doro wat. Their Tebsi dehro was good but not the best I've had. Their silsi dehro looked more like the real deal though. I would try this place again, and I would go with the silsi dehro.

Trekked out here for dinner from the outer boroughs, after having pleasant memories of good food and good service when my husband and I lived here more than 10 years ago... it was a busy Saturday night when we arrived, but we were seated promptly, with menus and water. Waitress came over, and asked, "Ready to order?" And I told her we wanted the Veggie Combo and Meat Combo to share. She looked at me, nodded her head, said "ok" and took the menus. We waited 1/2 hour... I asked her to check on our order. She said she would. 15 minutes later, she came over and asked if we had ordered already?!? I said yes, we had, right after we walked in. She claimed that she had asked me, in the beginning, right before she collected the menus, "Have you already ordered?" when she had said (and I had heard) no such thing. My husband and I got up and left, having to return to Queens with empty stomachs, since we only had the babysitter for another hour and had other family obligations that we could not be late for. What kind of system (table service-kitchen coordination) does a long-time restaurant have, that they could mess this up so badly? I hope this never happens again.
good service and food. a bit on the expensive side so don't know if I'd come back. it's more of an elevated dining experience

Perfect End To A Glorious Holiday Evening:

Had dinner here for first time,last night(12-17-23)
Had just attended the Candlelight Carol Festival at The Riverside Church along with a friend from Mumbai.He was thrilled when I told him I had made a dinner reservation at an Ethiopian restaurant.We are both vegetarian
From the moment we entered we were treated so well.The hostess was most friendly and accommodating and took the time to explain the menu and make suggestions.Our waiter as well was equally gracious.The menu has plenty of vegetarian/vegan options
The food was over the top and we are certain to return.I highly recommend

raw_place.title: Massawa
raw_place.description: East African eatery serves traditional Ethiopian & Eritrean fare scooped by hand with injera bread.
